population.title: Fix HangDump artifact paths for Windows directories with spaces
population.body:
HangDump quoted dump paths before calling `DiagnosticsClient.WriteDump` on Windows, then reused that quoted string for artifact publication. This produced `FileArtifact` paths containing literal quotes, which do not point to the dump file on disk.

- **Path handling**
  - Split dump path handling into two values:
    - quoted path for the Windows `WriteDump` workaround
    - unquoted path for `_dumpFiles` and artifact publication

```csharp
DumpFileNames dumpFileNames = GetDumpFileNames(finalDumpFileName);

diagnosticsClient.WriteDump(dumpType.Value, dumpFileNames.WriteDumpFileName, logDumpGeneration: false);
_dumpFiles.Add(dumpFileNames.ArtifactDumpFileName);
```

- **Regression coverage**
  - Added unit coverage for a Windows dump path containing spaces.
  - Verifies only the `WriteDump` argument is quoted and the artifact path remains unquoted.

population.title: feat(rsc): support custom server function directives
population.body:
## Summary

Adds an experimental `serverFunctionDirectives` API for framework directives such as Next.js-style `"use cache"`.

This is additive to the existing `rsc:use-server` implementation:

- the existing `vitePluginUseServer` transform remains in place
- custom directives run in a separate focused plugin immediately before it
- the only behavioral seam in `vitePluginUseServer` is preserving custom manifest metadata during cleanup and merging custom export names when a module also has `"use server"`

## API

```ts
serverFunctionDirectives: [{
  directive: /^use cache(?:: .+)?$/,
  test: (code) => code.includes("use cache"),
  filter: (id) => !id.includes("/node_modules/"),
  rejectNonAsyncFunction: true,
  validate({ directive, location }) {},
  filterExport({ name, meta }) {},
  wrap({ value, name, id, directiveMatch, location, hasBoundArgs }) {
    return `frameworkWrap(${value})`
  },
}]
```

## Reused functionality

The custom-directive plugin delegates to the same transform helpers used by `"use server"` for:

- inline scope/capture analysis and closure hoisting
- bound-argument encryption
- module export wrapping and proxy generation
- normalized server-reference IDs and manifest entries
- export-star expansion and export filtering

It also supports object methods, static class methods, destructured exports, named re-exports, stable custom hoist names, stateful regular expressions, and export filtering before async validation.

population.title: Fix pre-merge-commit hook to stage fixes when diagnostics remain
population.body:
## Summary

Fixes a bug in the pre-merge-commit hook where files modified by `mdsmith fix` were not being staged when the command exited with code 1 (indicating unfixed diagnostics remain). This caused merge commits to miss catalog regenerations and other auto-fixes on the merge queue.

## Root Cause

The original hook used `if ! mdsmith fix .; then` to conditionally handle exit code 1. However, the POSIX `!` operator returns the logical NOT of the command's exit status, so when `mdsmith fix` exits 1, the `!` makes it appear as 0 to the subsequent `$?` check. This caused the exit code guard to fail and the script to exit before reaching the staging loop.

## Key Changes

- **Hook script generation**: Changed from `if ! cmd; then status=$?` pattern to explicit `set +e / set -e` wrapping to capture the raw exit code before any shell operators can modify it
- **Exit code handling**: Updated the condition from `[ "$status" -ne 1 ]` to `[ "$status" -ne 0 ] && [ "$status" -ne 1 ]` to properly allow both success (0) and unfixed diagnostics (1) to proceed to the staging loop
- **Added regression test**: `TestBuildHookScript_StagesFixesWhenUnfixedRemain` reproduces the merge-queue scenario and verifies that modified files are staged even when `mdsmith fix` exits 1
- **Updated test assertions**: Modified existing tests to match the new hook script structure and verify correct exit code handling

## Implementation Details

The fix uses POSIX shell's `set +e` to temporarily disable the `set -e` error exit behavior, allowing the script to capture `mdsmith fix`'s raw exit status in a variable before re-enabling strict error handling. This ensures the staging loop always runs for exit codes 0 and 1, while still propagating unexpected error codes.

population.title: fix(types): keep overload set for imported @overload functions
population.body:
## Summary

Resolving `import from mod { fn }` collapsed an overloaded function to its **first** signature: `_set_module_item_symbol_and_type` set the import item's type from the primary symbol only and never gathered the sibling `@overload`s.

A call matching a *later* overload then failed. Real-world repro (SQLAlchemy):

```jac
import from sqlalchemy { create_engine }
glob eng = create_engine("sqlite:///:memory:");  # E1050: missing required parameter 'future'
```

`create_engine`'s first `@overload` makes `future: Literal[True]` required, so the checker rejected the single-arg call instead of falling through to the `**kwargs` overload.

## Fix

In `_set_module_item_symbol_and_type`, when the imported symbol is a function, gather its sibling overloads from the symbol's source scope (`collect_member_syms(sym.parent_tab, ...)`) and build an `OverloadedType` — mirroring the existing module-attribute path (e.g. `math.floor`).

## Test

`imported_overloaded_function_keeps_overloads` compiles a two-file fixture and asserts the imported function resolves to `OverloadedType` (2 overloads). Red before the fix (bare `FunctionType`), green after.

Earlier broader regression (298 checker/import tests) passed with this change.

## Note

This fixes the `E1050` false positive in the SQLAlchemy repro. A second, larger false positive in the same file — `result.rowcount > 0` (E1110), where `@util.memoized_property` isn't unwrapped via the descriptor `__get__` protocol — is a separate, tracked follow-up.

population.title: fix: run Code Blocks in the agent's authenticated browser context
population.body:
## Description
A workflow Code Block (running JS via the Playwright `page` — `page.goto` /
`page.evaluate`) does not run in the same authenticated browser context as the
preceding agent blocks. After a `login`/`navigation` block authenticates, the
next Code Block's `page.goto(<authed url>)` lands on the sign-in page, because
the block is handed a separate, unauthenticated browser. Reproduces with a
`login → code` (or `login → navigation → code`) workflow, with
`persist_browser_session` both on and off.
**Root cause.** Introduced with the v1.0.34 "script execution with browser
session state persistence" work. In a workflow run every browser-acquisition
path registers the authenticated `BrowserState` under the `workflow_run_id`
(agent tasks via `RealBrowserManager.get_or_create_for_task`, script bootstrap
via `get_or_create_for_workflow_run`). But Code Blocks run through
`Block.get_or_create_browser_state` in **both** live and script mode (the script
path's `skyvern.run_code` calls the same `CodeBlock.execute_safe`), and that
method consulted `PERSISTENT_SESSIONS_MANAGER` **first** whenever
`context.browser_session_id` was set — returning a different, unauthenticated
browser instead of the live one the agent already bound to the run.
**Fix.** `Block.get_or_create_browser_state` now (1) prefers the live
workflow-run browser (`BROWSER_MANAGER.get_for_workflow_run`), (2) falls back to
the persistent-session lookup only when there is no live browser (e.g. a
code-only run from the debugger), (3) otherwise creates one (unchanged). It's the
shared base-class path, so `PrintPageBlock` benefits too. No flag, no schema/DB
migration, no public-API change.

```diff
-        if browser_session_id and organization_id:
+        # 1. Reuse the agent's live, authenticated browser for this workflow run.
+        browser_state = app.BROWSER_MANAGER.get_for_workflow_run(workflow_run_id)
+
+        # 2. Fall back to a persistent session only when there is no live browser.
+        if not browser_state and browser_session_id and organization_id:
             browser_state = await app.PERSISTENT_SESSIONS_MANAGER.get_browser_state(browser_session_id, organization_id)
-        else:
-            browser_state = app.BROWSER_MANAGER.get_for_workflow_run(workflow_run_id)
```

This PR is independent of #<credential-test PR> and can merge in either order.
## How Has This Been Tested?
Environment: Python 3.11, `uv sync`, base commit at the `v1.0.36` tag.
- **Unit regression test** — `tests/unit/test_code_block_authed_browser_context.py`
  locks the browser-acquisition ordering. It fails on the pristine code (the Code
  Block receives the unauthenticated persistent browser) and passes with this
  change, so the regression can't silently return.
  `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_code_block_authed_browser_context.py` → 3 passed.
- **End-to-end Playwright proof (no LLM/server needed)** —
  `uv run python scripts/validate_code_block_auth_context.py` stands up an
  auth-gated mock site and drives real Playwright contexts: a fresh context hits
  `/dashboard` → sign-in page (reproduces the bug); reusing the agent's context →
  `page.evaluate()` reads the authenticated marker. Exit 0 == PASS.
## Artifacts (if appropriate):
N/A — covered by the unit test and the deterministic Playwright proof script above.

population.title: iOS: dismiss keyboard before opening Share sheet to prevent overlap
population.body:
On iOS Capacitor, exporting from a focused thought could open the Share UI while the software keyboard was still visible, causing the share surface to overlap and hide controls. This change updates the share flow so keyboard state is resolved before presentation.

- **Share flow ordering**
  - Ensures the active editable is blurred before invoking the native share action.
  - Defers share-sheet presentation until after keyboard dismissal has been requested.

- **iOS-specific guardrails**
  - Applies the keyboard-dismiss sequencing in the iOS Capacitor path to avoid regressions in non-iOS environments.
  - Keeps export/share behavior unchanged aside from presentation timing.

- **Behavioral outcome**
  - Share sheet now opens above app content without being occluded by the virtual keyboard.

```ts
// before triggering native share
if (isIosCapacitor()) {
  ;(document.activeElement as HTMLElement | null)?.blur()
  await dismissKeyboardIfVisible()
}

await presentShareDialog(payload)
```

population.title: Proof animation: render captions with an unclosed math delimiter
population.body:
## Problem

A derivation step's `operation` (or `justification`) occasionally arrives with an **unbalanced `$`** — the LM drops the closing delimiter, e.g.:

> Substitute `$V_{\text{lunar}} = 11 \text{ km/s}$` and `$V_{\text{LEO}} = 7.8 \text{ km/s}`  ← no closing `$`

`_caption` tokenizes on *balanced* `$…$`, so the first segment rendered but the tail showed as **raw LaTeX** in the caption and the Next pill (see the unrendered `$V_{\text{LEO}} = 7.8 \text{ km/s}`).

## Fix

Before tokenizing, balance an odd `$` (or backtick) count by appending the missing closer, so the trailing segment renders as math instead of leaking source. One-liner in `_caption`, no behavior change for already-balanced captions.

population.title: fix(security): JWT iss/aud validation + HS256 pin + UTF8 key (#29)
population.body:
## Summary
Closes #29 — **HIGH**: JWT validation gaps.

- The request-validation pipeline (`AuthorizationExtensions`) set `ValidateIssuer`/`ValidateAudience = false`, so any HS256 token signed with the shared secret was accepted regardless of issuer/audience — even though `AppJwtToken.Generate` stamps `iss`/`aud = "MechanicBuddy"`.
- `AppJwtToken` derived the key with `Encoding.ASCII` while the bearer pipeline uses `Encoding.UTF8` — a lossy mismatch for any non-ASCII secret.

## Changes
- Pipeline: `ValidateIssuer`/`ValidateAudience = true` with `ValidIssuer`/`ValidAudience = "MechanicBuddy"`; `ValidAlgorithms = [HS256]`; `ClockSkew = 30s`.
- `AppJwtToken`: `Encoding.ASCII` → `Encoding.UTF8` for both sign and validate.

## Verification
- `dotnet build -c Release` (Http.Api) succeeds (0 errors).

population.title: Prune stale FCM tokens on rotation
population.body:
## Summary
When FCM rotates a device's token, the old token is now removed from Firestore before the new one is added. This prevents token accumulation and ensures push targets stay clean.

Also unblocks the Firebase rules deploy workflow (issue #378) by populating `.firebaserc` with the production project ID and adding a fallback to the workflow's project resolution step.

## Changes
- **`src/services/fcm.ts`**: Added stale token pruning logic to `acquireAndStoreToken()`. When a new token differs from the cached one, the old token is removed from both `users/{uid}/private/profile` and `pushTargets/{uid}` via `arrayRemove()` before the new token is added. Removal is best-effort — failures are logged via `logger.warn` but never block the new token from being stored.

- **`src/services/__tests__/fcm.test.ts`**: Added three test cases:
  - Token rotation triggers removal of old token followed by addition of new token
  - New token is still stored even if stale removal fails (graceful degradation)
  - Re-acquiring the same token skips pruning entirely

- **`.firebaserc`**: Set `default` project to `sk8hub-d7806` to enable fallback project resolution in CI.

- **`.github/workflows/firebase-rules-deploy.yml`**: Enhanced project ID resolution to fall back to `.firebaserc` default when the `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID` secret is empty, with clearer error messaging.

- **`package-lock.json`**: `npm audit fix` bumps `hono` to clear moderate-severity advisories blocking CI.

## Implementation Details
- Stale removal is wrapped in a try-catch so a transient Firestore failure never prevents the new token from being stored
- Token comparison is explicit: only prune if `activeFcmToken` exists and differs from the newly acquired token
- Both Firestore documents are updated as separate best-effort `setDoc` calls (not a batch), consistent with the add path — the existing comment on L76-80 explains why batching mixed-permission docs is avoided

population.title: SFBL-260: fix duplicate_plan field-drops + dynamic regression test
population.body:
## Summary

\`duplicate_plan\` was hand-maintained and had silently fallen behind the schema, dropping four fields on duplication:

- \`LoadPlan.output_connection_id\` (SFBL-115/163) — clones reverted to local sink.
- \`LoadPlan.consecutive_failure_threshold\` (SFBL-121) — circuit breaker silently disabled.
- \`LoadStep.soql\` (SFBL-114) — query/queryAll steps lost their SOQL and were unrunnable on duplication.
- \`LoadStep.input_connection_id\` (incl. SFBL-178 \`local-output\` sentinel) — DML steps lost their input binding.

## Fix

Replace the hand-maintained copy with a \`_copy_columns(source, exclude)\` helper that iterates \`__table__.columns\` and excludes only identity/timestamp/structural columns:

- \`LoadPlan\`: \`{id, created_at, updated_at, name}\` (the new plan is intentionally renamed \`Copy of …\`).
- \`LoadStep\`: \`{id, created_at, updated_at, load_plan_id}\` (FK is rewritten to point at the new plan).

Any future column added to either model is now carried through automatically.

## Regression test

\`test_duplicate_plan_copies_all_columns\` builds a fully-populated source plan + step (every non-default column set to a distinctive value), duplicates it, and asserts dynamically against \`__table__.columns\` that every non-excluded column is preserved. The test will fail the moment a new field is added without the duplication helper being aware of it.

## Why this is its own PR

Discovered while expanding [SFBL-166](https://matthew-jenkin.atlassian.net/browse/SFBL-166). Surfaced as a blocker for SFBL-261 (the schema story) since the upcoming \`input_from_step_id\` work needs to ride on \`duplicate_plan\` too. Splitting it out keeps the epic PR focused on the named-step-outputs feature.

population.title: Unified login and single application shell (role-based)
population.body:
## Summary

Collapses the two separate sign-in experiences (admin portal login + employee portal login) into **one login page** and **one role-based application shell**, authenticating against **employee credentials**. This phase is scoped to identity/shell only — no approval-workflow, Department-Manager, language, or permission changes. Today's functionality and permissions are preserved exactly.

**One identity.** Employee credentials are now the canonical login. The legacy `admin/admin123` account stays only as a break-glass fallback inside the same form (no separate page/URL). A Super Admin who logs in with their employee credentials is bridged to the existing admin routers, so all admin functionality keeps working unchanged:

```
// server/_core/context.ts — synthesize an admin `user` for super_admin emp sessions
if (!user && empEmployeeId != null) {
  const emp = await getEmployeeById(empEmployeeId);
  if (emp && effectiveRoleOf(emp) === "super_admin")
    user = { id: emp.id, role: "admin", name: ..., /* User shape */ };
}
```

This means `protectedProcedure` / `adminProcedure` (keyed on `ctx.user`) require no changes and stay reachable only by super admins — branch managers/employees still cannot hit admin endpoints.

**One unified principal.** `auth.me` now returns a single principal used to drive the whole UI:

```
{ id, employeeId, name, firstName, lastName, email, jobTitle,
  role: "super_admin" | "branch_manager" | "employee", isManager, branchId }
```

resolved from the employee session (or the break-glass admin → `super_admin`). `auth.login` tries employee credentials first, then the admin fallback; `auth.logout` clears **both** session cookies.

**One shell.** `ERPLayout` is now the only shell with role-based nav groups:
- **Personal** (any employee): My Dashboard, Attendance, My Requests, New Request, Notifications (badge), Approvals (managers only), Change Password.
- **Administration** (super admin only): the existing ERP modules.

The employee self-service pages were folded into this shell by making `PortalLayout` a thin wrapper around `ERPLayout` (no per-page rewrites). `App.tsx` now has a single `/login`; the old `/emp/login` and admin login redirect to it. `ProtectedRoute` is super-admin-only (others redirected to `/emp`); `PortalRoute` serves personal pages to any authenticated employee. Notification deep-links (`/emp/manager?request=`, `/emp/requests?request=`) are unchanged since the `/emp/*` paths are preserved.

## Tests
- `npm test` → 47 pass (added a unified `auth.me` employee-session test; updated the two tests that asserted the old auth contract — `auth.me` role `admin`→`super_admin`, logout now clears both cookies).
- `npm run build` passes; `tsc --noEmit` at the same 21-error baseline (no new errors).

## Cutover note (not changed here)
Production data check (read-only): **Bader** is `super_admin` with active credentials; **Ali** is currently `erpRole = employee`. Ali must be promoted to `super_admin` before/at cutover or he'll sign in as a regular employee. Break-glass `admin/admin123` remains as a safety net regardless. Recommend running this as part of the deploy step (with approval).

population.title: Notification deep-links, attachment storage fallback, and role-based access control
population.body:
## Summary

Fixes the three leave-request issues reported during testing and adds a clean, enforced role model.

**1. Notifications now open the exact request.** Clicking a notification marks it read *and* navigates, deep-linked by request id:
- A manager's `request_submitted` notification → `/emp/manager?request=<id>` (opens the review box, scrolls into view, highlights the card).
- An employee's approval/rejection notification → `/emp/requests?request=<id>`.

```ts
function notificationTarget(n) {
  if (!n.requestId) return null;
  return n.type === "request_submitted"
    ? `/emp/manager?request=${n.requestId}`
    : `/emp/requests?request=${n.requestId}`;
}
```

**2. Attachments are no longer discarded.** Production (Render) has no object-storage proxy, so the old upload fallback returned a dead `/api/docs/<key>` URL and the bytes were lost. A new `persistUpload()` tries the proxy, then falls back to persisting the file in a new `uploaded_files` table; both upload paths (employee request attachments + employee documents) use it. Files are served by `GET /api/files/<key>` (legacy `/api/docs/*` kept for old URLs). The request details now show a clear "View / download attachment" link for both managers and employees.

```ts
// server/storage.ts
export async function persistUpload(relKey, data, contentType, filename) {
  try { return await storagePut(key, data, contentType); }
  catch {
    await db.putUploadedFile({ fileKey: key, filename, mimeType: contentType, dataBase64: data.toString("base64") });
    return { key, url: `/api/files/${key}` };
  }
}
```

**3. Role-based access control.** The 7-value `erpRole` enum is collapsed into the three account types and enforced consistently:

| Role | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| `super_admin` (Ali, Bader) | Everything — all branches, all requests |
| `branch_manager` | Their branch only |
| `employee` | Their own portal only |

- New `empManagerProcedure` gates the approval portal: requires an employee session whose effective role is `super_admin`, `branch_manager`, or a routed direct manager, and injects `role` + `branchId` into the context. Plain employees get `FORBIDDEN`.
- `getManagerRequestsScoped` / `canManagerSeeRequest` / `canReviewRequest` enforce branch boundaries: a branch manager sees and can act on requests only within their own branch (plus anything routed directly to them); a super admin sees all; other managers keep their per-report access so existing department-manager routing is unchanged.
- New `branchTeam` query returns a roster scoped to the manager's branch (super admin: all). The team queue is now name-enriched server-side, removing the portal's dependency on the admin-only `employee.list` endpoint (which previously 401'd for portal managers, showing "Employee #N").
- Client: portal sidebar shows a role badge; `ManagerPortal` shows a role-aware subtitle, a "branch team" panel, and an access-restricted screen for non-managers.

Note: the ERP admin console (the `users`/`admin` login) remains the Super Admin surface — its routers require a `users` session, which only the super-admin console grants, so branch managers/employees (portal sessions only) cannot reach admin APIs.

## Testing

- `npm run build` passes; `npx tsc --noEmit` reports 21 errors — identical to the pre-existing baseline, none from this change.
- `npm test`: 46/46 (added `server/rbac.test.ts` — 10 tests for role mapping + branch-visibility predicate).
- End-to-end run against a throwaway Postgres driving the real tRPC routers (20/20 checks): submit routes + notification carries `requestId`; attachment falls back to DB and is persisted/served; branch managers see only their branch; super admin sees all; employees blocked from the manager portal; cross-branch review blocked; branch-scoped team roster.

No production deploy or merge — held for review per the workflow.

population.title: Fix leave-request approval routing + UI polish (i18n names, employee row navigation, flat cards)
population.body:
## Summary
Two groups of changes:

### 1. Leave-request approval routing (root-cause fix)
Requests could be submitted but never reach a manager's approval queue (observed with employee Hadi, a dentist whose request never reached the branch manager). Root cause: **two divergent "who is my manager?" code paths**.

- Display (`employee.me`) resolved the manager with rich fallbacks: department manager → dentist-becomes-branch-manager → roll up to the top manager.
- Routing (`employeeRequest.submitRequest`) used **only** `department.directManagerId`, with no fallback.

So when a department had no `directManagerId` (e.g. **Dental**), a request was saved with `managerId = NULL`:

```ts
// before — submitRequest
const managerId = dept?.directManagerId || null;   // NULL for Dental
// getManagerRequests filters WHERE managerId = <manager> -> NULL matches nobody
// and `if (managerId)` skipped the notification entirely
```

The employee still *saw* a manager (a display-only, id-less fallback from `branches.managerName`), but the request was invisible to everyone and produced no notification.

Fix — a single source of truth used by display, routing, and the manager-portal gate:

```ts
// server/db.ts
resolveDirectManagerIdSync(emp, allEmployees, departments): number | null
// order: dentist -> branch manager (by role/job title, real id)
//        -> department.directManagerId -> ignore self -> top manager (super_admin)
resolveDirectManagerId(employeeId)        // async DB-backed wrapper
isManagerEmployee(employeeId)             // true if any active employee resolves to them
```

`employee.me` derives `directManager`/`isManager` from the resolver (so branch/top managers get the "Team Approvals" portal), and `submitRequest` routes via it — requests can no longer land with a NULL manager, and the notification always fires. No schema migration (branch managers matched by `erpRole`/job-title EN+AR). The full pending→approve/reject lifecycle was verified end-to-end (see Tests).

### 2. UI polish (follow-up requests)
- **Language consistency:** new `client/src/lib/i18n.ts` (`pickLang`/`employeeName`/`jobTitle`/`localizedName`) selects the field matching the active language with a fallback. Wired into Employees, EmployeeProfile, Branches, Tasks (lists, detail views, and `<Select>` dropdowns) so employee/manager/department/branch names follow the page language instead of mixing Arabic and English.
- **Employee row navigation:** the `/employees/:id` route and `EmployeeProfile` page already existed but nothing linked to them. Employees table rows now navigate to the profile on click; edit/delete buttons `stopPropagation` so they don't trigger navigation.
- **Card theme polish:** removed the hover-lift (`hover:shadow-md`/`transition-shadow`) from non-clickable informational cards (Dashboard stat cards, Tasks task cards). Clickable cards (Branches, BranchDetails — they have `cursor-pointer` + `onClick`) keep their subtle hover effect.

## Tests
- New `server/manager-resolution.test.ts` (9 cases): dentist→branch-manager (Hadi), department manager, branch-manager→top, top-manager→null, self-manager rolls up, dentist with no branch manager → top, no-department → top, Arabic job-title recognition, no-top-manager → null.
- Full suite green: 34 tests pass. `vite build` + `esbuild` server build succeed.
- **Controlled end-to-end run** against a throwaway Postgres seeded from a copy of production, driving the real tRPC routers (submit → route → manager queue → notification → approve/reject → authorization): **30/30 checks passed** across all departments/branches (Dental→Ahmed, Nursing→Roselyn, Administrative→Alhanouf, Management→Bader), incl. the Hadi case and a check that non-managers are blocked from reviewing. Confirms requests stay `pending` and visible until a manager approves/rejects.

population.title: feat(ios): integrate sing-box (Libbox) for real VPN traffic proxying
population.body:
## Summary

Replaces the non-functional packet loopback in `PacketTunnelProvider` with a real sing-box integration via Libbox. Previously the tunnel "connected" but didn't proxy any traffic — now it generates a complete sing-box config from the subscription URL and routes all traffic through the proxy servers.

### Core change: `PacketTunnelProvider` → Libbox

```diff
- // Old: loopback — packets go nowhere
- packetFlow.writePackets(packets, withProtocols: protocols)

+ // New: sing-box service handles all packet routing
+ let configJSON = SingBoxConfigBuilder.build(from: rawSubscription)
+ let service = try LibboxNewService(configJSON, self /* PlatformInterface */)
+ try service.start()
```

The provider implements `LibboxPlatformInterface`. The key callback is `openTun(_ options:) -> Int32` which:
1. Converts `LibboxTunOptions` → `NEPacketTunnelNetworkSettings`
2. Applies settings via `setTunnelNetworkSettings`
3. Scans for the UTUN file descriptor (`getsockopt(fd, SYSPROTO_CONTROL, UTUN_OPT_IFNAME)`)

### `SingBoxConfigBuilder`

Parses raw subscription lines and generates a complete sing-box JSON config:
- **Protocols**: VLESS (with Reality, XTLS flow), VMess (JSON + URI), Trojan, Shadowsocks, Hysteria2
- **Transports**: WebSocket, gRPC (`service_name`), HTTP/H2
- **TLS**: SNI, UTLS fingerprint, ALPN, Reality (public_key, short_id)
- **Config structure**: `tun` inbound → `selector` outbound → individual proxy outbounds, with DNS-over-HTTPS and auto-detect interface

### Other fixes

- **Duplicate logs**: `AppleVPNManager.logInfo` was writing to both `DebugLogStore` AND `os.log` — but `DebugLogStore.info` already calls `os.log` internally. Fixed to use one or the other.
- **App Group**: Added `group.uz.yeats.vpn` to both app and extension entitlements for shared container (sing-box working directory).

### Setup: building Libbox.xcframework

```bash
cd ios/YeatsVPN
./scripts/build-libbox.sh v1.13.13
# → Libbox.xcframework created
# Add it to the PacketTunnel target in Xcode (Embed & Sign)
```

Requires Go + gomobile on the build machine.

population.body:
## Summary
修复侧边栏宽度设置的两个缺陷：

1. **改动立即生效、无确认环节**：原 `SidebarWidthDialog` 的滑块/输入框/预设会直接调用 `onWidthChange` → `updateSetting('sidebarWidth', ...)` 立刻保存。
2. **宽度无上限**：`handleWidthChange` 只做 `Math.max(MIN, ...)`，输入框无 `max`。用户输入超大值（如 2000px）后侧边栏比视口还宽，把右上角的"宽度按钮"挤出可视区域，导致无法再次打开对话框恢复。

改动：

- **确认保存机制**：对话框改为本地草稿态 `draftWidth`，滑块/输入框/预设仅修改草稿，新增「取消 / 保存」按钮，仅点击「保存」才提交：
  ```
  const [draftWidth, setDraftWidth] = useState(() => clamp(currentWidth));
  // 打开时同步当前值
  useEffect(() => { if (open) setDraftWidth(clamp(currentWidth)); }, [open, currentWidth]);
  const handleSave = () => { onWidthChange(clamp(draftWidth)); onClose(); };
  ```
  点击遮罩 / 返回键 = 取消，不保存。

- **视口安全上限**：在 `sidebarOptimization.ts` 新增共享工具，保证宽度不会铺满屏幕，恢复入口始终可见：
  ```
  getSafeMaxSidebarWidth() = clamp(window.innerWidth - 120, MIN=340, MAX=800)
  clampSidebarWidth(w)     = clamp(w, MIN, getSafeMaxSidebarWidth())
  ```

- **已损坏状态自愈**：在所有读取宽度的入口套用 `clampSidebarWidth`，让已经保存了超大值、当前被卡住的用户重新打开应用即可恢复：
  - `ChatPageUI` 的 `getStoredSidebarWidth` 与 `appSettingsChanged` 监听
  - `SolidMotionSidebar` 的 `getStoredWidth` 与监听
  - `SettingsTab` 显示用的 `currentWidth`
  - `SidebarResizeHandle` 拖动时改用 `getSafeMaxSidebarWidth()` 作为上限

- `npx eslint` 改动文件无新增告警（`SolidMotionSidebar` 的 `set-state-in-effect` 报错为 main 既有问题）

## Description

Removes the `buildSpawnCommand` workaround that manually composed `cd` and env-prefix assignments into the command string client-side. population.title: fix(mastracode): detach from old thread PubSub on /new to prevent cross-instance output leak
population.body:
## Description

When two mastracode instances share the same `resourceId` (with `crossProcessPubSub` enabled), running `/new` in one tab caused it to continue receiving stream events from the old thread — so output from the other tab leaked into the `/new`-ed tab until the first message created a fresh thread.

**Root cause:** `/new` called `harness.abort()`, which only aborted the in-flight run but left the PubSub subscription active on the old thread's Unix-socket topic. The other mc instance's runs still published to that socket, and the stale subscription delivered those events to the TUI.

**Fix:** Add `Harness.detachFromCurrentThread()` which calls both `abort()` and `cleanupAgentThreadSubscription()` — fully unsubscribing from the old topic. `/new` now calls this instead of bare `abort()`. The `currentThreadId` is preserved so `createThread()` can still release thread locks when configured.

```diff
 // mastracode/src/tui/commands/new.ts
-  state.harness.abort();
+  state.harness.detachFromCurrentThread();
```

## Related issue(s)

Reported by @wardpeet in Slack (#mastracode) — two mc tabs on the same machine with different thread IDs sharing output after `/new` when no message has been sent yet.

## ELI5

Imagine you're playing a game on your computer, and you have two windows open for the same game. When you start a new game in one window, the other window was still listening to messages from the old game, so it kept getting confused by events happening in the first window. This fix makes sure that when you start a new game in one window, it stops listening to the old game's messages completely, so the windows don't interfere with each other anymore.

## Summary

This PR fixes a cross-instance event leakage bug in mastracode's TUI where running the `/new` command in one tab left the interface subscribed to the old thread's PubSub topic, causing events from other instances to leak into the new tab.

### Problem

When two mastracode instances shared the same resourceId with crossProcessPubSub enabled, running `/new` in one tab didn't fully unsubscribe from the old thread's event stream. While the command aborted the current run, it left a stale PubSub subscription that continued receiving stream events from other instances until the first message in the new thread created a fresh subscription.

### Solution

Added `Harness.detachFromCurrentThread()` method that performs a complete detachment by:
1. Calling `abort()` to cancel any in-flight operations and clear pending tool suspensions
2. Calling `cleanupAgentThreadSubscription()` to unsubscribe from the old thread's PubSub topic

The `/new` command now calls `detachFromCurrentThread()` instead of `abort()`. The current thread ID is preserved so `createThread()` can still release thread locks when configured.

### Changes

- **packages/core/src/harness/harness.ts**: Added public `detachFromCurrentThread(): void` method (+14 lines)
- **mastracode/src/tui/commands/new.ts**: Updated `handleNewCommand` to call `detachFromCurrentThread()` instead of `abort()` (+5/-3 lines)
- **mastracode/src/tui/commands/__tests__/new.test.ts**: Updated tests to validate the new `detach` call before `pendingNewThread` (+6/-5 lines)
- **.changeset/wide-buttons-kiss.md**: Patch release changelog entry (+6 lines)

## Description

Adds `@mastra/auth-neon` — an auth adapter for [Neon Auth](https://neon.com/docs/auth/overview), the managed authentication service built on Better Auth.

**Capabilities:**
- **JWT verification** via JWKS at `{baseUrl}/auth/jwks` (for API bearer tokens)
- **Session cookie verification** via Neon Auth REST API `GET /auth/get-session` (for Studio)
- **`ICredentialsProvider`** — email/password `signIn` / `signUp` via `POST /auth/sign-in/email` and `POST /auth/sign-up/email`
- **`IUserProvider`** — `getCurrentUser` from session, `getClearSessionHeaders` for logout
- **`ISessionProvider`** — session validate/refresh/destroy, cookie management
- **`MastraRBACNeon`** — maps Neon Auth org roles (`owner`/`admin`/`member`) → Mastra permissions via `roleMapping`, with LRU cache (60s TTL, 1000 size)
- Configurable `sessionCookieName` (default `neonauth.session_token`), `signUpEnabled`, and `jwksUrl` override

**Token flow in `authenticateToken`:**
1. Try JWKS JWT verification (stateless, fast)
2. If that fails, treat the token as a session cookie value → call Neon Auth session endpoint

```typescript
import { MastraAuthNeon, MastraRBACNeon } from '@mastra/auth-neon';

const mastra = new Mastra({
  server: {
    auth: new MastraAuthNeon({
      baseUrl: process.env.NEON_AUTH_BASE_URL,
    }),
    rbac: new MastraRBACNeon({
      roleMapping: {
        owner: ['*'],
        admin: ['*'],
        member: ['agents:read', 'workflows:*'],
        _default: [],
      },
    }),
  },
});
```

population.title: feat(core): validate EE licenses against the Mastra license server
population.body:
License validation for EE features now phones home to the license server (POST {MASTRA_LICENSE_URL}/validate)

## Description

License validation for EE features (RBAC, ACL, FGA, SSO) now phones home to the Mastra license server instead of validating keys locally.

**What changed**

- **New `LicenseClient`** (`packages/core/src/license`): validates via `POST {MASTRA_LICENSE_URL}/validate` (default `https://license.mastra.ai`), expecting `{valid, entitlements[], planTier, expiresAt, leaseTtlSeconds}` on success or `{valid: false, code, reason}` on rejection. Handles result caching for the lease TTL, background revalidation at 75% of TTL, a 72-hour grace period when the server is unreachable, and failing open while the first response is pending. Concurrent `validate()` calls coalesce into a single in-flight request, so startup makes one server call and logs one outcome.
- **`auth/ee` license helpers** are now a synchronous shim over the client's cached state. Public API is unchanged (`isLicenseValid`, `isFeatureEnabled`, `isEEEnabled`, `validateLicense`, `clearLicenseCache`, â¦) plus a new `startLicenseValidation()` that awaits the first server response.
- **Per-feature entitlement gating**: the `rbac`, `acl`, and `fga` capability flags now require their specific license entitlement via `isFeatureLicensed(feature)` (cloud, SimpleAuth, and dev environments remain exempt). `user`/`session`/`sso` keep the blanket license check.
- **`Mastra` constructor** fires a fire-and-forget validation on startup when a license key env var is set â it never blocks or throws during construction.
- **Env vars**: `MASTRA_LICENSE_KEY` is the new primary variable; `MASTRA_EE_LICENSE` still works as a deprecated alias (removal planned for a future release).

**Failure semantics** (design intent: license-server availability must never take down a customer's server)

| Scenario | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Key set, validation pending | Fail open until first response |
| Server rejects key | EE features disabled at runtime; running server keeps serving |
| No key + RBAC/FGA configured, production | Boot refused (existing behavior) |
| Server unreachable, previously validated | 72h grace period, then disabled |
| Server unreachable on first start | Fail open with 5-minute retry TTL |
| Dev environment (`NODE_ENV` â  production) | Exempt, no license required |

**Verification** â beyond the unit suite (110 tests, stubbed fetch), the full matrix was exercised end-to-end against the live licemode `mastra build` output: valid enterprise key (entitlements honored, RBAC/FGA enforced per role/rules), rejected key, missingkey, and unreachable-server fail-open.

population.title: ci: add workflow to build the app for all platforms
population.body:
## Summary

Adds `.github/workflows/build-app.yml`, a GitHub Actions workflow that builds the desktop client for **all platforms** on GitHub-hosted runners and uploads each build as an artifact. The existing `pr.yml` (and the Azure pipelines) only run on Microsoft's self-hosted `1ES` pools, so a fork has no runnable "build the app" workflow — this fills that gap.

Triggers: `workflow_dispatch` (manual) and pushing a `v*` tag.

Matrix (native arch per OS for reliability on hosted runners):

| platform | arch  | runner         |
|----------|-------|----------------|
| linux    | x64   | ubuntu-22.04   |
| win32    | x64   | windows-latest |
| darwin   | x64   | macos-13       |
| darwin   | arm64 | macos-latest   |

Each job mirrors the proven steps from `build/azure-pipelines/*/steps/product-build-*-compile.yml` and `pr.yml`:

```
setup-node (from .nvmrc)
(linux) apt install build-essential pkg-config libx11-dev libx11-xcb-dev libxkbfile-dev libnotify-bin libkrb5-dev
npm ci                      # ELECTRON_SKIP_BINARY_DOWNLOAD=1, retries x5
node build/lib/builtInExtensions.ts
npm run gulp vscode-${platform}-${arch}-min   # compile + minify + package
mv ../VSCode-${platform}-${arch} build-output/
upload-artifact
```

The `vscode-${platform}-${arch}-min` gulp task (defined in `build/gulpfile.vscode.ts`) is self-contained: it runs the build-with-mangling compile, extension/copilot compile, minify, and package steps, emitting `VSCode-${platform}-${arch}` into the parent of the repo dir — hence the `mv ../VSCode-...` before upload. `GITHUB_TOKEN` is passed to the `npm ci`, built-in extensions, and build steps because they download extensions from GitHub (anonymous requests get rate-limited).

## Notes / Testing
- YAML validated locally; `npm ci` succeeds locally. Full local build of the gulp task could not be completed on this machine because the built-in/marketplace extension download is rate-limited without a `GITHUB_TOKEN` (HTTP 403). In Actions, `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` is provided automatically, so this step works there — and the build commands match the already-working Azure pipeline steps.
- Adding a file under `.github/workflows/` will trip the repo's `no-engineering-system-changes` PR guard (inherited from upstream `microsoft/vscode`); this is expected for an intentional engineering-system change in your own fork.
- arm64 Linux/Windows are omitted to avoid flaky cross-compilation of native modules on hosted runners; the matrix can be extended later (e.g. `ubuntu-24.04-arm`).

population.title: fix(cli): preserve leading zeros in frontmatter during docs publish
population.body: ## Description Fixes frontmatter values with leading zeros being silently corrupted during `fern generate --docs`. When a page has `title: '001999'` in its MDX frontmatter, the published docs render the title as `1999`. ## Root Cause `parseImagePaths()` and `replaceImagePathsAndUrls()` round-trip frontmatter through `grayMatter()` → `grayMatter.stringify()`. Under the hood, `grayMatter.stringify` calls `js-yaml.dump()`, which has a subtle quoting bug: - Values with **only octal digits (0–7)** are correctly re-quoted: `'001015'` → `'001015'` ✓ - Values with **non-octal digits (8, 9)** are left **unquoted**: `'001999'` → `001999` ✗ When the downstream YAML 1.2 parser (in the docs rendering pipeline) sees bare `001999`, it interprets it as integer `1999` — leading zeros gone. ``` source: title: '001999' ↓ gray-matter parse data.title = "001999" (string, correct) ↓ grayMatter.stringify (js-yaml.dump) title: 001999 ← quotes dropped! ↓ YAML 1.2 parse in docs renderer title = 1999 (integer) ← leading zeros lost ``` This explains why mangopay error code pages `001015`, `000000`, `002601` (all-octal digits) rendered correctly, while `001999`, `009999`, `001599`, `002996–002998` (contain 8 or 9) were broken. ## Changes Made - Added `requoteLeadingZeroValues()` post-processing after both `grayMatter.stringify()` call sites in `parseImagePaths.ts` - The regex `^(\s*[\w][\w-]*:\s+)(0\d+)\s*$` matches only unquoted YAML values starting with `0` followed by more digits — the same values js-yaml failed to quote - [x] Unit tests added covering working (octal), broken (non-octal), and negative cases (normal numbers, bare zero) - [x] Changelog entry added ## Testing - [x] Unit tests added/updated — 6 new test cases covering the exact mangopay page values - [x] `pnpm turbo run test --filter @fern-api/docs-markdown-utils` passes - [x] Biome formatting verified **Note**: A complementary defense-in-depth fix exists in fern-platform (https://github.com/fern-api/fern-platform/pull/12126) at the rendering layer. This CLI fix prevents the data corruption at the source so FDR stores correct frontmatter going forward. population.body: ## Summary 排查「首页点卡片打开帖子弹窗比搜索联想打开卡顿」：骨架屏尺寸传递（`coverAspectRatio` → `coverHint` → skeleton `aspect-ratio`）本身实现正确，不是卡顿来源。真正差异是首页路径独有的已读标记——`goPost` 在 280ms 后重建整个 `list` 数组，触发 VirtualMasonry 布局重算 + 全部可见卡片 patch，恰好与 PostOverlay 挂载、详情/评论数据回填渲染撞在同一时间窗（联想路径没有这步，所以流畅）。 改法：网络请求 `markAsReadBatch` 仍点击时立即发出（不占主线程），本地 list 重建推迟到弹窗关闭后——弹窗期间卡片被完全遮住，用户看不到已读变化： ``` goPost: pendingReadIds.add(id); api.markAsReadBatch([id]).catch(() => pendingReadIds.delete(id)) watch(postModal.isOpen → false): setTimeout(flushPendingReadIds, 320) // 等离场动画结束 flushPendingReadIds: 一次性合并所有 pending id 重建 list（仅有变化时） ``` 请求失败时从 pending 移除即可（不再需要原来的乐观回滚）；弹窗期间连开多帖也只在关闭后重建一次。 Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/a83c6dfdc3474622b8a1f88d0feae116 Requested by: @KawaYiLab ---

population.title: fix(zzzui): respect prefers-reduced-motion for breathing animations
population.body:
## Summary

用户反馈 `zzzui/packages/menu/menu-item.vue` 的激活菜单项「两种颜色快速互相变换」。排查结论：这不是渲染 bug，而是 zzzui 设计系统刻意的「呼吸」高亮——激活态元素通过 `z_ani_*` 无限动画在黄 `#ffea00` ⇄ 绿 `#91bc00` 间循环（`menu.scss:46`），`ease-in-out` 让它在两端停留、中段快切，看起来像闪烁。稳态/正常交互下动画平滑且多组件同步，无异常抖动。

本 PR 按「无障碍方案」处理：在 `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` 下停掉这种持续的颜色/尺寸呼吸（永不停止的高对比颜色循环正是对动效敏感用户的「闪烁」来源，此前 zzzui 完全没适配该偏好），同时修掉 `animate-sync.js` 一处相位判断缺陷。默认（无偏好）行为完全不变。

## Changes

**`zzzui/packages/theme/animation.scss`** — 在 `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` 下重定义呼吸关键帧为「平帧」，使动画无视觉变化但保留静态高亮（不能直接 `animation: none`，否则激活项背景会整个消失）。功能性 loading 旋转 `z_ani_loading` 保留。

```scss
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  @keyframes z_ani_background { from, to { background: $--gradient-yellow; } }
  @keyframes z_ani_color      { from, to { color: $--gradient-yellow; } }
  /* border_color / outline_color 同理；size 类压平为 scale(1) / outline 2px */
}
```
> 选黄色 `#ffea00` 作为静态色：激活项文字为黑色，黄底对比度优于绿底。

**`zzzui/src/utils/animate-sync.js`**
- 减少动效偏好下直接不启动 rAF 同步循环（省掉常驻 rAF）：
```js
export const startAnimationSync = () => {
  if (typeof document === 'undefined') return
  if (prefersReducedMotion()) return   // 新增
  if (rafId !== null) return
  rafId = requestAnimationFrame(animationSync)
}
```
- 修复参考相位判断：原 `colorCurTime ? ... : ...` 在 `currentTime === 0` 时把「已记录参考」误判为「未记录」。改为显式 `=== null`：
```diff
- colorCurTime ? (item.currentTime = colorCurTime) : (colorCurTime = item.currentTime)
+ colorCurTime === null ? (colorCurTime = item.currentTime) : (item.currentTime = colorCurTime)
```

## Verification

通过 CDP 用 Playwright 模拟两种偏好，采样真实 `<z-menu>` 激活项的 `backgroundColor`：
- `no-preference`：逐帧变化 `rgb(247,231,0)`→`rgb(197,210,0)`（黄→绿，照常呼吸）。
- `reduce`：恒为 `rgb(255,234,0)` = `#ffea00`，8 帧不变（无闪烁，高亮保留）。

`npx nuxi typecheck` 通过；仓库无 lint / 无单测文件 / 无 CI workflow。

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/4ac40bed9d6b419da5337449127b319c
Requested by: @KawaYiLab

population.title: Refine theme presets: collapsed UI, mode-aware presets, trimmed list
population.body:
## Summary
Follow-up to the unified Theme & Customization panel. Cleans up preset UX and fixes the "light sidebar in dark mode" bug.

**Presets are now mode-aware.** Each curated preset declares `mode: 'light' | 'dark'` and applying it switches the app's dark-mode accordingly, so a light theme never renders on top of dark mode (and vice-versa) — that was the broken light sidebar in the screenshots.

```ts
const applyUnifiedPreset = (preset) => {
  if (preset.mode && preset.mode !== (isDarkMode ? 'dark' : 'light')) toggleDarkMode();
  ...
}
```

**Presets now also drive font, corner radius and glass.** `PALETTE_PRESETS` configs were colors+sidebar only; each now also sets `fontFamily`, `borderRadius`, `glassIntensity` so picking a preset restyles the whole look, not just colors.

**Collapsed by default.** The presets grid shows only 3 (active one first) with a "Show all N themes" toggle; the Customize/advanced controls are now behind a collapsible header (`showCustomize`, default closed).

```
[ active ] [ #2 ] [ #3 ]
   Show all 6 themes  v
> Customize  (colors, font, radius, glass & sidebar)   v   <- collapsed
```

**Trimmed the list.** Dropped the 6 legacy accent-only `data-theme` presets (Notion Minimal, Midnight Forge, Golden Hour, Neon Pulse, Nordic Frost, Forest Growth) and the redundant palettes (Retro Blues, Tokyo Neon, Warm Editorial), leaving 6 curated presets (3 light / 3 dark). `LEGACY_ACCENT_CONFIG` and the legacy branch of `applyUnifiedPreset` were removed.

Custom saved presets also capture the current `mode` so re-applying restores light/dark correctly.

population.title: Unify theme & customization settings panel and fix sidebar styles
population.body:
## Summary

The Appearance settings previously had **two overlapping theming sections** — an "Advanced Theme Settings" preset grid and a separate collapsible "Custom Theme Designer" (which itself had its own redundant palette-preset grid). This merges them into a **single "Theme & Customization" panel** and fixes the broken sidebar style variants.

### Unified panel (`SettingsView.tsx`)
- One card: a **Presets** grid on top, an always-visible **Customize** section below (Colors, Font, Corner Radius, Glass Effect, Sidebar Style), then the actions (Apply & Save / Save as Preset / Reset). No more collapse-to-find-the-controls.
- All preset sources are merged into one grid via a single `applyUnifiedPreset(preset)` handler:
  ```
  unifiedPresets = [
    ...ENGINE_PALETTE_PRESETS (built-in palettes, incl. sidebarStyle),
    ...BASE_THEME_PRESETS      (legacy accent themes -> LEGACY_ACCENT_CONFIG),
    ...customPresets           (user-saved),
  ]
  ```
  Legacy accent-only themes (`midnight`, `forest`, …) are mapped to a `Partial<ThemeConfig>` so they still apply through the same `applyThemeConfig` path instead of the old `data-theme` swap — nothing is dropped. Active selection is tracked with `activePresetId` (persisted to `forge_active_preset`) so every preset, including palettes/customs, now shows a check + active ring.
- Sidebar Style options now render a small visual sketch (`SidebarStylePreview`) per option instead of an ASCII glyph.

### Sidebar style fixes (`index.css`, `App.tsx`)
- **Island**: nav icons were forced to `opacity: 0` (replaced by a tiny dot), making the rail unusable — you couldn't tell items apart. Icons are now visible; the active item gets a centered underline pill that fits the floating card.
- **Dock**: the floating dock could cover page content (e.g. the Apply & Save button on full-bleed pages). Added `padding-bottom` to `#main-content` on desktop when dock is active, and added the missing **Widgets** tab to the dock.
- **Expanded**: the active item lost its text label because the base `.nav-pill-active::after` repurposes `::after` as a left bar (the same pseudo-element used to render the label). Active items in expanded mode now keep their label. `DroppableTab` also forwards `data-label` so the Calendar item is labeled.

### Notes
- `npm run lint` (`tsc --noEmit`) reports 86 **pre-existing** errors on `main` (in `server.ts`, `FloatingChat.tsx`, `DirectSearch.tsx`, etc.); none are in the files touched here. `vite build` passes.

population.title: Implement browser-based Battleship (Human vs AI) per FINAL_BATTLESHIP_SPEC.md
population.body:
## Summary

Full implementation of the Battleship game described in `FINAL_BATTLESHIP_SPEC.md`, built in four reviewed phases (core logic → tests → UI → config/build/docs). React 18 + TypeScript + Vite + TailwindCSS, tested with Vitest.

Verification (all green):
- `npm test` → **30/30** passing
- `npx tsc --noEmit` → no errors
- `npm run build` → succeeds; JS bundle ~47 KB gzipped (target < 300 KB)

### What's here

- **`src/lib/`** — pure, React-free logic:
  - `game.ts`: `isValidPlacement` (bounds + row-wrap via `Math.floor(start/10) !== Math.floor((start+len-1)/10)` + overlap), `placeShip` (max 1000 tries, throws on failure), `placeAllShips` (`[5,4,3,3,2]` → 17 cells), `isAllShipsSunk` (spec's `for…of` early-return), `initializeGame`.
  - `ai.ts`: `getAIMove` — collect cells `0–99` not yet attacked, return random, throw when none left.
  - `types.ts`: `GameState` + supporting types.
- **`src/components/`** — `Cell.tsx`, `Board.tsx`, `Game.tsx` built exactly to spec.
- **`tests/game.test.ts`** — all required suites (`isValidPlacement`, `placeShip`, `placeAllShips`, `isAllShipsSunk`, `getAIMove`, `initializeGame`).
- Config: `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `tsconfig.node.json`, `tailwind.config.js`, `postcss.config.js`, `netlify.toml`, `index.html`, `src/main.tsx`.
- `README.md` and `BUG_LOG.md`.

### Spec invariants enforced

- Flat indices `0–99` only — no x/y or 2D arrays.
- Immutable updates — every state change builds a `new Set(...)`; no mutation.
- Guard clause order in `handlePlayerAttack`: `phase !== 'playing'` → `currentTurn !== 'player'` → `playerAttacks.has(index)`.
- `useEffect(…, [game.currentTurn, game.phase])` — never `[game]`; 600ms AI delay.
- Grid via `Array.from({ length: 100 }, …)` — never `[...Array(100)]`.

### Deviations from spec file list (documented in `BUG_LOG.md`)

These were required to make the spec's own commands runnable; file *contents* match the spec where provided:
- Added `jsdom` to devDependencies — `vite.config.ts` sets `environment: 'jsdom'` but it was absent from the dependency list, so Vitest couldn't start.
- Added `/// <reference types="vitest" />` to `vite.config.ts` so the `test` block typechecks (Vite's `defineConfig` doesn't type it).
- Added `tsconfig.node.json` — referenced by the spec's `tsconfig.json` but its contents weren't provided.

`README.md` still has the `[DEPLOY_URL_HERE]` placeholder; will fill in once deployed to Netlify (not part of this PR).

population.title: fix: critical fixes — city autocomplete, rate limiting, cart clearing
population.body:
## Summary

Three critical fixes from the gap analysis, targeting checkout reliability, LLM token budget, and UX polish.

### P2: Fix broken city autocomplete (checkout flow)

`DeliveryCityAutocomplete.fetchCities` was calling `/api/chat` (full LLM chat endpoint) and parsing the streamed response as city names — unreliable and wasteful.

```diff
- fetch("/api/chat", { body: { messages: [{ content: `List delivery cities matching "${query}"` }] } })
- const text = await res.text(); // parse LLM stream as city names 😬
+ fetch(`/api/cities?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}`)
+ const data = await res.json(); // { cities: string[] }
```

New `GET /api/cities?q=...` route calls `kapruka_list_delivery_cities` MCP tool directly and returns structured JSON.

### P1: Rule-based intent classification (halve LLM calls)

Added `classifyIntentByRules(message)` as a fast path before the LLM classifier in `orchestrate()`. Common queries matching regex patterns (shopping keywords, delivery/logistics, order/checkout) skip the `streamText` classifier call entirely — saving 1 LLM call per message on the free tier's 150 req/day budget.

```
"show me cakes"       → shopping  (rule-based, no LLM call)
"deliver to Colombo"  → logistics (rule-based, no LLM call)
"place my order"      → order     (rule-based, no LLM call)
"hello"               → null      (falls back to LLM classifier)
```

### P9: Clear cart after order

`handlePlaceOrder` now dispatches `CLEAR_CART` after constructing the order message, so the cart empties immediately on order submission.

### Tests

Updated `orchestrator.test.ts` with new `classifyIntentByRules` test suite (5 test cases) and updated existing `classifyIntent`/`orchestrate` tests to verify rule-based fast path skips LLM calls. All 84 tests pass.

population.body:
## Summary

Adds folder-based organization to the Notes section. Users can assign notes to folders (e.g., "Meetings", "Setup/Dev Environment"), filter by folder via a sidebar tree, and manage folders through the create/edit dialog. Notes without a folder appear under "Uncategorized."

**Backend:**
- Flyway migration (`V2`) adds nullable `folder` TEXT column + composite index on `(user_id, folder)`
- `folder` field added to entity, all DTOs (Create, Update, Response, Filter)
- 5 new repository query methods to support folder filtering, including combined tag+folder queries
- `NoteService.list()` expanded with 6-branch filter matrix (tag × folder × uncategorized combinations)
- New `GET /api/notes/folders` endpoint returns distinct folder names for the current user
- `list()` and `listForUser()` controller methods accept optional `folder` query param

**Frontend:**
- NotesPage reworked with a 240px folder tree sidebar (All Notes → Uncategorized → nested folder tree)
- Folder tree parses flat paths (e.g., `"Setup/Dev Environment"`) into a collapsible hierarchy
- Folder Autocomplete (`freeSolo`) in create/edit dialog for selecting existing or typing new folders
- Folder chip displayed on note cards; folder selection persisted in URL search params
- "+" button to create folders via `window.prompt`

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Verify the 6-way filter branching in `NoteService.list()`** — the `isUncategorized` check is evaluated before `hasFolder`, which is important because `"__uncategorized__"` is non-empty and would match `hasFolder` too. Confirm all 6 branches produce correct queries.
- [ ] **Test folder tree with intermediate nodes** — if only `"Setup/Dev Environment"` exists as a folder, clicking the parent "Setup" node in the tree will filter for `folder=Setup`, which has no notes. Decide if this is acceptable UX or if parent nodes should aggregate children.
- [ ] **Empty string → null folder handling consistency** — `create()` uses `request.getFolder() != null && request.getFolder().isEmpty() ? null : request.getFolder()`, while `update()` uses a simpler `request.getFolder().isEmpty() ? null : request.getFolder()` inside a null guard. Both work, but the asymmetry is worth noting.
- [ ] **E2E test**: Create notes with/without folders, switch between folder sidebar items, verify filtering works with tag+folder combinations, edit a note to move it between folders, and confirm "Uncategorized" shows only folder-less notes.

### Notes
- No backend or frontend tests were added — the filter matrix in particular would benefit from unit tests.
- No folder name validation exists — arbitrary strings (including very long or special-character names) are accepted.
- The `__uncategorized__` sentinel is a magic string passed through the API; a user creating a folder literally named `__uncategorized__` would collide with this behavior.
- TypeScript compilation and Java compilation both pass cleanly.

## Two small fixes

### 1. Bug: history entries missed the provider
`src/routes/Review.svelte` recorded visited PRs into the recent-reviews history without the `provider` field, so GitLab/Bitbucket entries on the landing page navigated via the github fallback (wrong URL). The provider is now persisted on the history entry at record time (`addToHistory({ provider: prRefX.provider, ... })`).

- Migration: legacy entries without `provider` keep the github fallback (unchanged behavior, `entry.provider ?? 'github'` in Landing).
- Tests: history record asserts `provider: 'github'` by default and `provider: 'gitlab'` when Review is mounted with the gitlab provider (GitLab REST shapes stubbed); Landing already covers navigation of a gitlab history entry to `/review/gitlab/...`.

### 2. Flaky test EC-05k — root cause + fix
**Root cause:** `App.svelte` lazy-loads the Review route via dynamic `import()`. In vitest, the FIRST test to hit a `/review` route (EC-05k in file order) pays the module transform + instantiation of the entire diff-view dependency graph (@git-diff-view, lowlight/highlight.js, marked) *inside* testing-library's 1s default `findBy*` window. Under CPU contention (parallel test files in a full-suite run, loaded machine) that exceeds 1s and the `findByText(/CLOSED-PR/)` times out.

**Proof:** reproduced deterministically by saturating all cores — 6/6 runs failed before the fix (EC-05k plus the three PR-ONE lazy-route tests), 0/6 after, under identical load. 10/10 consecutive clean runs in normal conditions (before and after merging main).

**Fix (cause, not retries):** a `beforeAll` in `App.test.ts` pre-warms `import('./routes/Review.svelte')` so the one-time compile cost is paid outside any assertion window — the tests measure rendering behavior, not module-transform latency. The bundle-discipline test remains valid: even with a warm module cache, dynamic `import()` resolves asynchronously, so the `.route-loading` fallback still shows synchronously after render. (Main independently landed generous 10s timeouts on the same `findBy` calls; both coexist — the pre-warm removes the variance, the timeouts stay as defense in depth.)

population.title: Plan G part 2: agentic deep review — verification tools for the AI reviewer (opt-in)
population.body:
## Summary

Single-pass reviewers flag unverified suspicions. This PR gives the model **tools** to verify each suspicion before flagging — improving precision on the two precision-critical paths: **skill-reviewer runs** and the **verdict** task. Opt-in via a new **Deep review (agentic)** toggle (default off) because the loop costs more tokens. Toggle off = byte-identical behavior to today (all pre-existing tests untouched and green).

Plan doc: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-13-review123-plan-g-agentic-review.md`

## What's inside

- **`llmToolLoop()`** (`src/lib/llm/llmToolLoop.ts`, alongside llmComplete/llmStream): sends tool definitions, executes the model's tool calls, appends results, repeats until a final schema'd answer or the budget exhausts (then disables tools and demands the final answer). Usage summed across rounds — the `llm*WithUsage` / PostHog token-event pattern keeps working.
- **Tools** (`src/lib/ai/deepReview.ts`): `read_file` (PR head), `read_file_at_base`, `search_code` (GitHub code-search scoped to the repo; capability-gated by `ReviewProvider.searchCode?` method presence — GitLab/Bitbucket simply don't offer the tool yet). Budgets: **max 8 tool calls, max 150 KB fetched** per run, 50 KB/file with an explicit truncation marker.
- **Failure honesty**: tool errors (404, rate limit, budget) feed back as tool-result errors so the model proceeds without; transport failures mid-loop surface the existing error rendering — never a spinner hang.
- **Caching**: deep results cache under keys with a `\`|deep\`` marker (+ PROMPT_VERSION), wrapped with `toolCallsUsed` so the footer survives cache hits. Partial loops never cached.
- **UI**: live tool-activity lines ("Reading src/foo.ts…", "Searching: createPrLoad…") under the verdict skeleton and in the skill run-status bar; finished cards show "Deep review: verified with N tool calls"; honest fallback note when the model lacks tool support.
- **Prompting**: deep-mode system suffix — form hypotheses from the diff, verify with tools before flagging, drop anything unverifiable — composed on top of the v10 calibration blocks from #78 (re-merged and composed, not clobbered).

## Per-transport notes

| Transport | Wire format | Forced final answer |
|---|---|---|
| openai-compat (DeepSeek direct + OpenAI proxy) | `tools` / `tool_calls` / `role:"tool"` | `tool_choice: "none"` |
| anthropic | `tools` + `tool_use` / `tool_result` content blocks (`is_error` on failures) | `tool_choice: {type:"none"}` |
| gemini | `functionDeclarations` + `functionCall` / `functionResponse` parts | `functionCallingConfig.mode: "NONE"` |

**DeepSeek function-calling status (verified 2026-06-13 against api-docs.deepseek.com):** supported on `deepseek-v4-flash`, `deepseek-v4-pro`, and `deepseek-chat` via the OpenAI-compatible shape. Legacy `deepseek-reasoner` historically does not support function calling → flagged `supportsTools: false`; with the toggle on it falls back to single-pass with an honest UI note.

- `deepReview.test.ts` — 18 tests: tool list gating, truncation marker, 150 KB run budget, 404/exception honesty, humanized strings, availability gate

population.title: Fix OAuth callback misdispatch (GitHub sign-in failing with GitLab error) + GitLab navbar parity
population.body:
## Bug: settings-initiated GitHub sign-in failed with a GitLab error

**Root cause.** `/auth/callback` dispatched on *"does a GitLab pending-session key exist?"* (`getPendingProvider`), and `review123:gitlab-oauth` is only cleared when the GitLab completer actually runs. A GitLab sign-in attempt abandoned **before** the callback (e.g. GitLab rejects the redirect URI, user presses Back on the consent screen) left that key behind. The next GitHub sign-in wrote its own `review123:oauth` session but did **not** clear the stale GitLab one, so the callback routed to `completeGitlabSignIn`, the GitHub `state` nonce failed the stale GitLab state check, and the user saw *"GitLab sign-in session expired or invalid"*. It looked settings-specific because the GitLab button lives in settings — any tab that had ever abandoned a GitLab attempt reproduced it; fresh tabs (typical navbar usage) did not.

**Fix (mechanism level).**
- **Single shared `beginOAuth()` helper** (`src/lib/auth/oauthFlow.ts`) used by *all* entry points — navbar, settings `ProvidersSection`, and `VerdictStep`. It clears both pending sessions before starting a flow and stores `review123:returnTo`. No duplicated pending-state writes anywhere.
- **Dispatch by state nonce**: `resolvePendingProvider()` matches the callback's `state` against each pending session first (the fresh flow always wins, even if a stale key survives), falls back to the single pending session for error callbacks without `state`, and returns `null` when nothing matches — the callback then shows a provider-agnostic error and clears leftovers instead of blaming the wrong provider.
- **Error copy names the provider actually attempted** (e.g. "GitHub sign-in session expired or invalid", not GitLab's).

## Navbar provider status parity

- GitLab now appears next to GitHub: **"GitLab ✓" + sign-out** when connected, **Sign in with GitLab** (official-style `GitLabSignInButton`) when `VITE_GITLAB_CLIENT_ID` is set but not connected, and **nothing** when the env var is absent (env-gated like elsewhere).
- Sessions stay independent — GitLab sign-out clears only `gitlabOAuth`.
- Compact below 700px: sign-in buttons collapse to icon-only chips and sign-out buttons to an `✕` chip (accessible names preserved via `aria-label`).

## Tests

- `oauthFlow.test.ts`: begin-flow stale-clearing + dispatch matrix (github-pending, gitlab-pending, stale-then-fresh both directions, no-state fallback, ambiguous → null, malformed JSON).
- `AuthCallback.test.ts`: dispatch regressions incl. stale-gitlab + fresh-github → GitHub completer with GitHub-named error copy.
- `App.test.ts`: navbar GitLab parity (env-gated, connected/expired states, independent sign-out both directions).
- e2e (`settings.spec.ts`): full settings-initiated GitHub round-trip with a stale GitLab session re-seeded on every document load — authorize redirect and `/api/oauth/exchange` route-intercepted; navbar parity + compact-below-700px test. Playwright `webServer` now bakes e2e client ids so the env-gated buttons render in the preview build.

## Note on GitLab "redirect URI not valid"

That error is GitLab-side app config: the OAuth application's registered redirect URIs must include **every origin the app is served from** (production domain *and* localhost for dev). Our `redirect_uri` derivation from `location.origin` is correct. Documented in the README's GitLab OAuth setup section.

population.body:
Four user-reported settings fixes from live usage.

## 1. Show/hide eye toggle on API key fields
- New shared `SecretInput.svelte` (inline SVG eye/eye-off, no new dependency): masked ↔ plain text, `aria-label` "Show key"/"Hide key", `aria-pressed`, themed icon button.
- Used by all four provider key fields in **AiModelsSection** and the GitHub PAT / GitLab token / Bitbucket token fields in **ProvidersSection** (Bitbucket *email* stays a plain masked field — not a token).
- Keys are never logged or captured; the toggle only flips the input type locally.
- **Latent bug fixed en route:** the Advanced `<details>` used a one-way `open={derived}` attribute that Svelte's grouped template effect re-applied on *any* state change — typing one character in any advanced field snapped the panel shut. Now `bind:open` with user-owned state (regression test included).

## 2. Key sanitization + friendly errors
User hit `Window.fetch: Cannot convert value ... character at index 49 has value 8212` — an EM DASH (U+2014) copy-paste artifact in a saved DeepSeek key blew up fetch header construction. Fixed at two levels:
- **Save path:** shared validator (`findInvalidKeyChar` / `invalidKeyCharMessage` in `settings.ts`) trims whitespace and rejects non-ISO-8859-1 / control characters across **all** key/token fields (AI provider keys, GitHub PAT, GitLab token, Bitbucket email+token — both go into the Basic auth header) with: `Key contains an invalid character ("—" (U+2014) at position 50) — re-copy it from the provider.`
- **Transport (belt-and-braces for keys saved before this fix):** `mapFetchError` in `llm.ts` detects the header-construction `TypeError` (Firefox ByteString / Chrome Invalid value / WebKit invalid header wordings) and maps it to the same human message instead of surfacing the raw DOMException text. Generic `Failed to fetch` still maps to `network`.

## 3. Provider-aware "Generate from my reviews" copy
The gate copy *looked* hardcoded to DeepSeek because `hasAiKey` / `aiProviderName` derived from a non-reactive `getSettings()` snapshot frozen at mount (default: DeepSeek). Now derived from the reactive `settingsState` facade: switching provider or saving a key updates the gate live, and the copy reads `Add an API key for <Provider> (see AI models above) to use this feature.` Audited SkillsSection + AiPanel for other stale DeepSeek strings — none remained.

## 4. Scrollspy can't select Appearance at the top
Root cause: the midline rule picks the *last* section whose top is above the viewport midline — at scrollTop ≈ 0 the page header pushes the short Appearance section's successor above the midline, so "Providers & access" was highlighted while reading Appearance. Fix in `pickActiveSection`:
- While the **first section's top edge is still at or below the viewport top**, the first section wins. Geometry-based (no `scrollY`), so it cannot be fooled by a scroll-container vs window mismatch, and it self-adapts to the header height (no magic threshold).
- Checked before the at-bottom override so a page that fits the viewport starts on the first section; bottom edge still reaches the last section.
- Added a passive scroll listener in SettingsPage: IntersectionObserver only fires on threshold crossings, so the last few pixels toward an edge could leave the active item stale.

- 2890 unit tests pass (≈ +127 on this branch incl. merged main), `svelte-check` clean, `pnpm build` clean.
- 63 e2e pass / 1 skipped (real-network smoke), including 2 new e2e: eye toggle + em-dash friendly error, and scrollspy top/bottom/top walk.

population.title: Anti-fatigue calibration of all review-output prompts (PROMPT_VERSION 10)
population.body:
## Why

User verdict on current AI review output: "insanely verbose, flagging moot points (causing fatigue), texts feel redundant — the goal is value-add, not mental drain." This PR calibrates every review-output prompt for signal over volume.

## Calibration rules encoded (adapted per prompt)

1. **Evidence gate** — only flag what can be cited (file:line in the diff) AND with articulated concrete harm ("what breaks / who gets hurt"). Bare "consider… / might want to… / ensure that…" without a stated failure mode is banned; unverifiable harm → "couldn't verify" or silence, never assertion.
2. **Hard caps** — at most 5 skill findings / 5 hotspots / 5 test gaps / 5 verdict evidence bullets per run, ranked by severity × confidence, with a one-line "(N lower-confidence observations omitted)" note when candidates are cut.
3. **Brevity format** — one sentence WHAT+WHERE, one sentence WHY IT MATTERS, optional ≤1-sentence fix. No restating the diff, no praise padding, no methodology narration.
4. **Silence is a valid answer** — empty findings/hotspots/gaps/alternatives arrays are explicitly framed as a GOOD, expected outcome on clean code.
5. **No redundancy** — the skill-review path now receives existing PR comment bodies (≤30, truncated to 200ch — same policy as the coach) with a "never repeat a point an existing comment already makes" instruction.
6. **Severity honesty** — nits are nits; severity must never be inflated, so the severity-colored cards (PR #68) reflect real stakes.

## Per-prompt summary

| Prompt | Changes |
|---|---|
| `skillReviewPrompt` | Full rule set; cap 15→5 (schema's 15 validator unchanged, kept as parse backstop); existing-comments dedupe section; all-clear framing |
| `attentionPrompt` | Cap 5 hotspots; two-sentence reasons; omission note; empty-hotspots-is-good; shared block |
| `verdictPrompt` | Cap 5 one-sentence evidence bullets; no diff restating; shared block |
| `testInsightPrompt` | Behaviors = one ≤15-word sentence; gaps capped at 5 with concrete-harm requirement + "General: N lower-confidence observations omitted"; shared block |
| `alternativesPrompt` | approach ≤2 sentences; tradeoffs ≤2 sentences (one gain, one cost); empty-array-is-good; shared block |
| `summarizePrompt` | Keeps ~120-word cap; adds no-padding/no-narration/no-diff-restating line |
| `builtinSkills.ts` (6 personas) | One shared `SHARED_CALIBRATION` block appended to all personas — no per-persona rewrites |

## Cache invalidation

**PROMPT_VERSION 9 → 10.** All cached task results (including skill reviews, whose cache key combines PROMPT_VERSION with the skill content hash) are invalidated on deploy — users will see a fresh, calibrated run per PR. JSON schemas are unchanged, so any stale v9 cached entries that survive still parse.

## UI

Zero-finding reviewer runs now render a one-line **"✓ no significant issues"** chip instead of "✓ 0 findings"; verified the empty findings array renders no cards, buttons, or summary lines.

population.title: feat(sis): SIS ID anchor + student profile import/export (DO NOT MERGE - staging review)
population.body:
**DO NOT MERGE YET — staged for Marv's review per the mission.** Branch preview deploy = staging.

# SIS ID Anchor + Student Profile Import/Export

`school_student_id` becomes the first-class, unique-per-school anchor on the student record — the school-issued number that survives email changes, provider switches, and teacher rotation. Provider identities (`external_identities`) hang off it. This is the structural backbone of the longitudinal claim.

## Phases (each live-tested against Westview on prod)
1. **Migration 075** (applied to prod ✓): anchor columns + partial unique index, `roster_imports` + `roster_import_rows`, `get_my_role()` helper, admin-only RLS (`TO authenticated`, no `USING(true)` hole). **Backfill 0 by design** — `sis_external_id` is a provider UUID, not the school-issued number; it stays a match hint.
2. **LmsConnector extension**: `capabilities` / `importStudentProfiles` / `exportStudentProfiles`. GC adapter: real server-side paginated `students.list`; `supportsSisId: false` (GC carries no SIS number); export not-supported. `applyImportedStudentProfile` = THE single roster identity+anchor path; **provider sync never overwrites a differing anchor** (conflict queue; 23505 race degrades to conflict). Invariant matrix unit-tested.
3. **CSV roster import** (`/admin/rosters/anchor-import`): SheetJS (.csv/.xlsx), column auto-detect + mapping UI, five-status preview (status pills), apply-matched-only, idempotent, never creates accounts. Live: 30-row CSV hit all five statuses; re-upload converged; teacher 403; audited.
4. **Match review** (`/admin/rosters/match-review`): three queues, side-by-side compare incl. current-holder context, confirm/pick/skip, no bulk-resolve, stale-row escalation guard, indigo "X of Y anchored" readiness stat. Same-filename re-uploads supersede stale queue rows. Live: all actions + audit verified; Westview ended 8/9 anchored.
5. **Profile export** (`/admin/profile-export`): versioned shared serializer (`{version: 1}` — future OneRoster push reuses it), CSV+JSON keyed on anchor with `anchor_missing` flags, school-scoped (cross-school 404 proven live), audited, locked excludes (no IEP, no numeric risk score, no narrative caches, no Teli transcripts) verified against real output.

## Phase 6 checklist — all 13 pass
Uniqueness 23505 ✓ · single roster path (grep: `captureRosterIdentity` only inside `applyImportedStudentProfile`) ✓ · never-overwrite invariant ✓ · five statuses + idempotency ✓ · zero account creation ✓ · review actions audited ✓ · stat 7/9→8/9 ✓ · export scope + cross-school 404 + audit ✓ · excludes verified in real output ✓ · `school_student_id` absent from URLs/logs/Sentry/PostHog allow-list (grep + Zod registry inspection) ✓ · silent-SSO regression: `resolve_external_identity` resolves real prod identity rows correctly (note: `leila@student.core.com` doesn't exist on prod; verified with actual GC identity rows) ✓ · teacher RLS: API 403s + direct table read RLS-empty + write 42501 ✓ · suite 1,983 green ✓

## Zero-to-anchored (pilot playbook, 5 lines)
1. School connects Google Classroom (or just uses CORE) — students exist, no IDs yet.
2. Admin downloads a roster export from their SIS — any SIS, the file always has the student ID.
3. Upload at **Student ID import** → preview shows exactly what will happen → Apply (most students anchor instantly by email).
4. **Match review** clears the tail: confirm name suggestions, resolve any conflicts — watch "X of Y anchored" climb.
5. Done: every signal now compounds against an ID that survives everything; **Profile export** proves the record is portable any day they ask.

population.title: Dashboard: country filter dropdown on all statistics pages
population.body:
## What

Adds a **country dropdown** next to the time-range pills on every `/dashboard/*` statistics page, carried as `?country=SE` in the URL so the selection persists when switching tabs — same pattern as `range`.

## How it works

- **Country source of truth:** `dashboard_workshops.country` (ISO-2 from the codeoc export), inherited per user via `dashboard_users.workshop_id` (836/837 users link to a workshop). Dropdown options are the countries that actually have app users, ordered by user count.
- **New `src/lib/ceo/countries.ts`:** param normalization, cached dropdown options, and `loadCountryFilterSets()` returning the country's user/workshop id sets for loaders to filter with.
- **New `DashboardShellNav` client component:** tabs + range pills + country select read/merge the current URL client-side, so no page has to thread searchParams into the shell. Side benefit: range pills now preserve page-local params (platform, q, status) instead of dropping them.

## Pages with live filtering

| Page | Filtered via |
|---|---|
| Feature Usage | login + feature rows by user→country map |
| Active Users | user union by user→country map (GA4 rows are per-user) |
| Top Lists | users via active-users; cars via diagnostics user/workshop |
| Usage | GA4 `countryId` dimension filter (IP-geo) + diagnoses by workshop country |
| New Users | sign-ups/activations by user/workshop; store + GA4 download columns show "—" (no user identity, can't be attributed) |
| Diagnostics | item workshop country |
| Workshops | workshop country |

Sections with no country attribution (Domain Health, Reviews, Email Campaigns, CTA Clicks, Conversions, the test pages, …) show the dropdown disabled with a "not applied here" hint; the URL keeps the selection for when you tab back.

Loader caches now key on `(range, country)`; the Update buttons still bust everything via `revalidateTag("ceo-data")`.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint` clean
- `vitest run src/lib/ceo` — 9 files, 85 tests pass
- `next build` from the worktree passes

Jacob linked the "Trial-ending reminder" touchpoint (marked *Idea — doesn't exist*) to a **running** Customer.io campaign — proof the original audit's email-side facts were assumptions (the audit could read app code, not Customer.io). The board should verify itself.
