population.title: fix(pwa): stop persistent update banner; gate on ready SW update
population.body: ## المشكلة رسالة «نسخة جديدة من تقفيلة» كانت تظهر باستمرار لأن: 1. الاعتماد كان **فقط** على مقارنة `/api/v1/meta` مع build العميل — بدون التحقق من وجود Service Worker جاهز للتفعيل. 2. الفحص يُعاد عند **كل** عودة للتبويب (`visibilitychange`). 3. على VPS البناء يتم بدون `.git` فمُعرّف الإصدار قد لا يكون مستقرًا بين العميل والخادم. ## الحل ### شروط ظهور احترافية - يظهر البانر فقط عندما: - يوجد **waiting service worker** (تحديث حقيقي جاهز) - **و** build الخادم أحدث من build العميل الحالي - **و** المستخدم لم يضغط «لاحقًا» لنفس build - زر **لاحقًا** يخفي الرسالة لهذا الإصدار (sessionStorage) - فحص الخلفية مُقيّد (كل 5 دقائق) + الاستماع لأحداث `updatefound` من SW - عند تطابق builds يُمسح dismisal تلقائيًا ### استقرار build على الإنتاج - تمرير `GITHUB_SHA` كـ `RELEASE_BUILD` أثناء `pnpm build` على VPS - توحيد قراءة build في `/api/v1/meta` (بدون fallbacks متضاربة) - حفظ `RELEASE_BUILD` في `.env.production` ## Verification - `corepack pnpm check:refactor` ✅ (809 tests + smoke)

population.title: fix: canonical paths, broker demotion gating, transactional safety
population.body: ## Summary Fixes three post-v0.9 issues: macOS symlink path asymmetry, capability broker demotion without runtime enforcement, and transactional worktree safety. ## Changes ### 1. `canonicalPath()` — realpath asymmetry (P0) Adds `canonicalPath()` in `path-utils.ts`: resolve symlinks for the longest **existing** prefix, append non-existent suffix unchanged. Used across path-utils, allowlist, diff-evaluator. ### 2. Capability broker demotion tied to runtime `capability_fs_hint` demotion uses `isCapabilityBrokerDemotionActive()` → `hasSandboxRuntime()`. ### 3. Transactional safety - Skip when tracked files are modified (`dirty_worktree`) - `transactional_apply_failed` on apply errors (deny, no host re-execution) - **Apply rollback** — partial `copyFile` failures roll back earlier files best-effort - `resolveWorktreeCwd` uses `canonicalPath` for symlinked repo roots ### CI - `verify-macos` job (`macos-latest`, `pnpm test`) ## Review fixes (latest) - `capability-approval.test.ts` asserts `canonicalPath('/tmp/...')` (fixes macOS `/private/tmp` CI failure) - `resolveWorktreeCwd` canonical path mapping + rollback tests ## Tests - 231 tests passing locally

population.title: feat: v0.9 capability broker and control-plane isolation (L1-full path)
population.body: ## Summary Implements **v0.9 — Capability broker & control-plane isolation** from the [v0.7–v1.0 plan](docs/v0.7-v1.0-plan.md). Belay does not implement OS sandboxes itself; this release adds the **configuration path and approval broker** for L1-full when an external sandbox runtime enforces deny-all. ## What's new - **`sandbox` config (opt-in)** — `enabled`, `runtime` (`none` | `cursor-sandbox` | `container` | `seatbelt` | `landlock`), `denyNetworkByDefault` - **FS capability broker** — `fs-scope-allowlist.json`; outside-repo shell rules demote to `capability_fs_hint` when paths are allowlisted - **`agent-belay approve --scope path --path `** — persist outside-repo allowances (parallel to egress `--scope domain`) - **`controlPlane.isolation`** — `none` | `read-only-mount` | `separate-user` with `verifyControlPlaneIsolation()` used by doctor/sandbox status - **`agent-belay sandbox status`** — reports broker state, isolation health, and L1-full prerequisites - **Layer conformance matrix** — tests for `l3-l4-only`, `l1-partial-egress`, `l1-l2-transactional`, `l1-full` profiles - **[`docs/guarantee-table.md`](docs/guarantee-table.md)** — per-configuration guarantees (adversarial claims only for L1-full) ## Review fixes (latest commit) - `l1FullActive` now requires `sandbox.runtime` ≠ `none`, not only `sandbox.enabled` - FS-scope allowlist no longer treats a child path entry as approval for its parent directory - One-shot shell approvals no longer bypass outside-repo rules while the sandbox broker is active (`--scope path` required) - Added capability approval, gate runtime, and L1-full conformance tests ## L1-full prerequisites All required for `l1FullActive: true`: 1. `sandbox.enabled` + real external runtime (`runtime` ≠ `none`) 2. `egress.enabled` + proxy running for this repo 3. `controlPlane.isolation.mode` ≠ `none` 4. `approvalSigning.required: true` ## Enable (example) ```json { "sandbox": { "enabled": true, "runtime": "container", "denyNetworkByDefault": true }, "egress": { "enabled": true, "demoteL3External": true }, "approvalSigning": { "required": true }, "controlPlane": { "isolation": { "mode": "separate-user", "verifyAgentWritable": true } } } ``` ## Tests - 224 tests passing (`pnpm test`)

population.title: PROD-106: checkout round-trip + Customer Portal (web PWA)
population.body:
The user-facing checkout flow on top of [PROD-104](https://linear.app/bellskill/issue/PROD-104) (checkout session) and [PROD-105](https://linear.app/bellskill/issue/PROD-105) (webhook) — the last Phase-2 piece. Paywall → Stripe Checkout → back into the app with premium active, plus a Customer Portal entry. Web-only (native link-out deferred to PROD-107).

**Gating decision:** the real Subscribe CTA is behind `features.premium`. Production carries **live** Stripe keys, so until launch the paywall keeps the existing **notify-me** CTA; flipping `VITE_FEATURE_PREMIUM=true` at launch turns on real checkout. This PR is safe to merge without charging anyone.

**Changes:**
- **Paywall** (`PaywallPage.tsx`): selectable monthly/yearly cards (yearly preselected) + a single **Subscribe** CTA → `useCreateCheckoutSession` → `window.location` redirect to Stripe Checkout. When `features.premium` is off, the notify-me CTA is unchanged.
- **Return routes** (always routed): `/checkout/success` calls `useEntitlement().refetch()` and **polls through the webhook race** (~2s × 8) with a calm "it'll update shortly" fallback — never an error or trap; `/checkout/cancel` returns to the paywall, no guilt.
- **Account**: "Manage Subscription" (shown when `isPremium`) → new **`create-portal-session`** Edge Function → Stripe Customer Portal, returning to `/account`.
- `useCreatePortalSession` hook; `config.toml` + both CI workflows deploy the portal function. No new secrets (reuses `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `SITE_URL`).

**Testing:**
- Unit: gated CTA (Subscribe vs notify-me by mocking the flag) + plan-selection label; `CheckoutSuccessPage` pending→premium; `CheckoutCancelPage`. **Full suite 256/256**, `tsc` clean.
- `create-portal-session` verified locally: 400 without a Stripe customer; a real `billing.stripe.com` portal URL with one (confirms the Customer Portal is enabled in test mode).
- Checkout-session redirect and webhook premium-flip were already verified in PROD-104/105.

**Manual check before/after merge (DJ, optional):** with `VITE_FEATURE_PREMIUM=true` locally + `stripe listen`, run `npm run dev` → `/paywall` → Subscribe → pay `4242…` → `/checkout/success` flips to premium; cancel path; Account → Manage Subscription round-trip.

**After this merges**, Phase 2 is complete end-to-end. Premium launch is a separate step: trial backfill, `VITE_FEATURE_PREMIUM=true` in prod, and shipping the real gated feature.

population.title: PROD-105: stripe-webhook Edge Function (sole writer of subscription state)
population.body:
The webhook that keeps Supabase in sync with Stripe — the **sole writer** of the subscription state columns ([PROD-105](https://linear.app/bellskill/issue/PROD-105)). Closes the loop [PROD-104](https://linear.app/bellskill/issue/PROD-104) left open: completing a payment now flips the user to premium. Phase 2 (web-only). No client changes.

**Changes:**
- `supabase/functions/stripe-webhook/index.ts` — authenticated by the **Stripe signature** (`verify_jwt = false`), verified off the raw body via `constructEventAsync` + SubtleCrypto. Handles:
  - `checkout.session.completed` → maps by `client_reference_id`, (re)links `stripe_customer_id`.
  - `customer.subscription.updated` / `deleted` → maps by `stripe_customer_id` (these carry no `client_reference_id`, which is why PROD-104 persisted it).
  - On every event it **re-fetches the live subscription from Stripe** and writes the authoritative state via the **service role**, making handling idempotent and safe against replayed / out-of-order events (no schema change).
  - **`past_due` keeps premium**; downgrade to `free` only on terminal states → cancel-at-period-end stays premium until the `deleted` event at period end.
  - Per-event logging (`event.id`, type, user/customer, outcome).
- `supabase/config.toml` — `[functions.stripe-webhook]` with `verify_jwt = false`.
- Both CI workflows now also `supabase functions deploy stripe-webhook`.
- `.env.example` documents `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (local value from `stripe listen`).

**Testing (local, real Stripe test subscription + self-signed events):** drove a real test subscription on a real customer and posted properly-signed webhook events. **11/11 checks passed:**

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Bad signature | 400 |
| `customer.subscription.updated` (active) | → premium by customer mapping; `has_premium_access = true`; `stripe_subscription_id` stored |
| `checkout.session.completed` | → premium by `client_reference_id` |
| `customer.subscription.deleted` | → free; `has_premium_access = false` (re-fetch saw `canceled`) |
| Replay deleted event | no state change (idempotent) |

`past_due` (keeps premium) is covered by the `active`/`past_due → premium` mapping, bracketed by the verified active→premium and canceled→free cases.

**Out-of-band before this works in deployed envs (DJ):** register the Stripe webhook endpoint per mode → `https://<project>.supabase.co/functions/v1/stripe-webhook` (events: `checkout.session.completed`, `customer.subscription.updated`, `customer.subscription.deleted`), and set `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` per environment in the Supabase Dashboard. The CI deploy step runs on merge regardless (function just won't verify events until the secret is set).

population.title: PROD-104: create-checkout-session Edge Function (Stripe, web PWA)
population.body:
First Supabase Edge Function in the repo — the server side of paywall checkout ([PROD-104](https://linear.app/bellskill/issue/PROD-104)), part of Phase 2 (web-only PWA; Capacitor deferred). Creates a Stripe Checkout Session for a premium subscription. Webhook (PROD-105) and the CTA→redirect→return flow (PROD-106) are separate tickets.

**Changes:**
- `supabase/functions/create-checkout-session/index.ts` — authenticated endpoint. Derives the user from the JWT (never trusts a body-supplied user id), maps `{plan: monthly|yearly}` → price id from env (never trusts a client price). Creates/reuses the Stripe customer and writes `stripe_customer_id` via the **service role** (that column is write-locked from clients); the webhook owns the rest of the subscription state. Returns the Checkout URL with `client_reference_id = user.id`; success/cancel URLs point at `/checkout/*` web routes (built in PROD-106).
- `supabase/functions/_shared/cors.ts` + `create-checkout-session/deno.json` — establish the Edge Function convention (shared CORS, per-function import map).
- `supabase/config.toml` — `[functions.create-checkout-session]` with `verify_jwt = true`.
- `src/api/useCreateCheckoutSession.ts` — client invoke hook (exported; **not yet wired to the paywall CTA** — that's PROD-106).
- Both CI workflows now `supabase functions deploy create-checkout-session` after `db push` (they previously only pushed migrations).
- `.gitignore` + `.env.example` for the local function secrets; no Stripe key is in the repo.

**Testing (local, up to the Stripe call):**
| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| OPTIONS preflight | 200 + CORS header |
| No `Authorization` | 401 |
| Valid JWT + invalid plan | 400 (auth + validation run pre-Stripe) |
| Valid JWT + valid plan (dummy key) | reaches `stripe.customers.create()` → `StripeAuthenticationError` |

The last case proves the full path is wired (authed user → service-role profile read → Stripe call), failing only on the placeholder key. Full happy-path with a real test key (open Checkout URL, verify `client_reference_id` + `stripe_customer_id` written) is run separately with secrets set. App test suite: 251/251; client typechecks clean.

**Deploy note:** the new `functions deploy` CI step runs on merge; it deploys fine even before runtime secrets are set (the function just 500s until they exist), and nothing is user-facing yet (CTA is still notify-me). Secrets are set via the Supabase Dashboard, not committed.

population.title: Paywall v1 (Phase 1): trial infra, entitlement gating, paywall screen
population.body:
Phase 1 of the [PROD-99](https://linear.app/bellskill/issue/PROD-99) paywall epic — trial infrastructure, entitlement gating, and the paywall screen. Premium unlocks future AI features; the free tier keeps logging, skill tree, and analytics. Every user gets a 30-day full-access trial. **Payments are not wired in this PR** (Phase 2 = Stripe, Phase 3 = Apple — both out of scope and blocked on external setup + Capacitor, which isn't installed).

Closes PROD-100, PROD-101, PROD-102, PROD-103.

**Changes:**
- **DB (PROD-100):** `supabase/migrations/20260612000000_add_subscription_entitlement.sql` adds subscription columns to `profiles`, the `has_premium_access(user_id)` function (single source of truth: `tier='premium' OR (trial_ends_at IS NOT NULL AND now() < trial_ends_at)`), and **column-level INSERT/UPDATE locks** so clients cannot write subscription state — only the service role (Phase-2 webhook) can.
- **Entitlement layer (PROD-101):** `useEntitlement` hook with a pure, tested `deriveEntitlement()` that mirrors the SQL rule; `EntitlementContext` provided app-wide in `App.tsx`; `PremiumGate` component. Client gating is UX-only — the authoritative gate is server-side RLS + `has_premium_access`.
- **Trial lifecycle (PROD-102):** `TrialStatusPill` (hidden until ≤7 days, emphasized in the final 48h) on the Account page; graceful auto-downgrade at expiry. The premium-launch backfill lives in `supabase/manual/` and is intentionally **not** auto-deployed — it runs once at launch (everyone gets a fresh 30-day clock).
- **Paywall (PROD-103):** `PaywallPage` with trial-aware variants (trialing / expired / free), \$9.99·mo or \$79·yr pricing, honest copy, and a notify-me CTA (Phase-2 checkout seam left in place).
- Placeholder gated `RecommendationsPage` behind the `premium` feature flag so the gate→paywall flow is real and testable.

**Security note (caught in review):** the original migration only locked `UPDATE`. Because `profiles` also has INSERT + DELETE RLS policies, a user could have deleted and re-inserted their own row with `subscription_tier='premium'` to self-grant premium. The migration now locks INSERT with column-level grants too — verified that escalation inserts are rejected while legitimate `ensureProfile` inserts still succeed.

**Testing:**
- 13 new unit/integration tests (entitlement derivation across all 4 states, `PremiumGate`, paywall variants, notify-me CTA). Full suite: **251/251 green**.
- `tsc` clean for all changed files; project lint unaffected.
- Verified against local Postgres (rolled-back transactions): `has_premium_access` returns correct results for active-trial / expired / premium / free; the column-level write-lock blocks `subscription_tier` updates **and** inserts while leaving `username` edits and legitimate profile inserts working.

**Follow-ups before merge:** run `npm run gen:types` to regenerate `types/supabase.ts` (columns were hand-added to keep TS compiling). The migration deploys via the existing GitHub Actions path on merge. The `recommendations` route/nav are gated behind `VITE_FEATURE_PREMIUM` (off by default).

population.title: fix(security): unblock attestation on ignored esbuild GHSAs
population.body:
## Summary

The 0.1.4 CLI release dispatch failed on `Run repo security attestation`: esbuild <0.28.1 picked up two advisories today (GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr, Deno-module-only RCE; GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr, Windows-only dev-server file read). Neither code path is reachable in this repo, and the patched esbuild 0.28.1 is blocked by `minimumReleaseAge` until ~2026-06-15, so this ignores both advisories with a tracked removal plan instead of punching through the supply-chain age guard.

## Changes

- `pnpm-workspace.yaml`: `auditConfig.ignoreGhsas` for the two esbuild advisories, with expiry comment
- `.trivyignore` + `.grype.yaml`: same two GHSAs, preemptive (their DBs will ingest the advisories soon)
- `scripts/lib/pnpm-audit-policy.mjs` (+tests): pnpm 10.19 ignores `ignoreGhsas` when computing the exit code (it derives from `metadata.vulnerabilities`, which still counts ignored advisories), so the attestation now gates on the post-ignore advisories list. Fails closed on unparseable/malformed output.
- `scripts/security-attest.mjs`: `evaluateStatus` hook on `runStep`; records `raw_status` when the policy overrides the exit code; writes `pnpm-audit-policy.json` evidence
- `docs/ops/security-todo.md`: checkbox to remove all three ignores and bump esbuild >=0.28.1 once it clears the age window (~2026-06-15)

population.title: Summon: route a group chat to the owner's main DM session via /summon
population.body:
## What

Lets the owner temporarily pull their main `dm:<identity>` session (full personal memory and context) into a group chat, instead of the group's own isolated session.

- `/summon` (in a group) — the sender's main session takes over the group. Owner-gated via a provider-verified sender id (Telegram `from.id`, iMessage handle address); display names are never trusted.
- `/dismiss` — hand back to the group's own session.
- Auto-handback after `summonExpiryMinutes` of group inactivity (default 60, `0` disables, `TOMO_SUMMON_EXPIRY_MINUTES` env override).
- `/status` shows the active summon.
- State persists in `~/.tomo/data/summons.json` and survives daemon restarts.

## Reply model: nothing auto-posts to the group

Summoned group messages arrive in the dm session tagged `[group "Title"] Sender: ...`. The turn's direct reply target stays the owner's **private DM** — group-facing replies happen only via an explicit `send_message(mode=direct)` tool call with the group's session key. This makes coalesced batches and steered messages audience-safe by construction: a merged or mixed turn can't deliver to the wrong audience because the only path into the group is an explicit, per-message tool call.

The model is briefed in four layers: a pending note on summon/dismiss/expiry, the per-message group tag, a per-turn reply-routing reminder (prompt-only, kept out of transcripts), and an audience-switch note injected whenever consecutive inbound messages hop between the private DM and a group (or between groups, or mix within one batch).

## Key routing details

- `IdentityRouter.resolve()` is the single choke point: summoned groups resolve to the dm key, so group and DM traffic automatically serialize on one `LiveSession`.
- The group is never persisted as the dm session's reply target — cron/continuity keep delivering to the private DM.
- Group participant/title tracking stays keyed by the raw group key while summoned, so the group's own session stays fresh for handback.
- Summon expiry is lazy (detected on the next routing lookup, no timer); it posts a handback notice to the group and a pending note to the dm session.

## Docs

Design notes, privacy model, and open questions (per-turn reminder cost, multi-owner groups, `/new`-in-group semantics) in `docs/summon-spike.md`. `defaults/AGENT.md` gains a "Summoned Groups" section teaching the reply flow.

## Testing

- `npm run build`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` — 437 tests pass.
- New tests: summon routing + expiry (`tests/router.test.ts`), `SummonStore` persistence/expiry (`tests/summon-store.test.ts`), audience-switch notes (`tests/audience.test.ts`).

population.title: Keep subagent events out of channel delivery and turn state
population.body:
## What

Stop subagent events (those carrying `parent_tool_use_id`) from reaching the user-facing channel or polluting turn state in `LiveSession`.

## Why

`handleEvent` treated subagent events the same as the main agent's. Since all channel delivery hangs off `currentRequest` (`onText` / `onBlockComplete`), a subagent's interim narration would:

- **leak to the user as Tomo's own words** when a turn happened to be in flight as the block arrived (and it hit the `!hadStreamDeltas` path, so the *entire* block got pushed into the streamed message), or
- **get silently swallowed** when no request was in flight (text pushed into `parts`, then cleared at the next `send()`).

Which one you got depended purely on arrival timing relative to the in-flight turn — which is exactly why the leak looked nondeterministic on iMessage (one subagent message leaked, the next didn't). Steering makes the leak *more* frequent because steered messages widen the in-flight window.

## Change

`handleEvent` now branches on `parent_tool_use_id` at the top:

- Subagent events route to an observability-only `logSubagentEvent` — tool activity is still logged (tagged `subagent: true`), but `parts` / `streamingText` and the channel-facing callbacks are never touched.
- Subagent replay echoes can no longer false-match steer merge detection.

Behavior is now deterministic: subagents never speak to the user directly; their outcome reaches the user only when the main agent folds the `Agent` tool result into its own reply.

## Testing

- Two new `LiveSession` tests: subagent narration (text blocks + stream deltas) stays out of callbacks and the resolved response; subagent replay echoes don't trigger steer merges.
- Full suite green: **413 tests pass**, `tsc` build clean.

## Background

This came out of investigating whether the SDK's native `run_in_background` could let you keep chatting with Tomo while a background subagent runs. Findings (verified with throwaway probes, since removed):

1. In long-lived `query()` mode, `run_in_background` holds the parent turn open until the subagent finishes — non-blocking for the model's reasoning, but the conversation turn stays busy.
2. The `steering` feature (#142) bridges this: a subagent's tool calls act as injection boundaries, so a mid-turn message gets answered *while* the background task is still running.
3. Exercising that path surfaced this subagent-leak bug, which this PR fixes.

population.title: Add message steering to inject mid-turn messages into in-flight turns
population.body:
## Summary

Implements experimental message steering (`config.steering`) to inject user messages into an in-flight turn instead of queueing them behind it. This enables more responsive interactions when the agent is processing a long-running turn.

## Key Changes

- **LiveSession refactor**: Replaced single `pendingMessage` callback with a queue-based input system (`inputQueue`, `inputWaiter`) to support concurrent message injection
  - Added `STEER_MERGED` sentinel constant for steered messages that merge into the in-flight turn
  - New `steer()` method injects a message at the next tool-call boundary; if the turn has no boundary left, the CLI queues it as a follow-up turn
  - Tracks three request states: `currentRequest` (turn owner), `mergedRequests` (steered messages echoed mid-turn), `pendingSteers` (injected but not yet seen)
  - Added `isBusy()` to detect when a turn is in flight (including promoted steered turns)

- **Request lifecycle management**:
  - `failTurn()` centralizes rejection of the owner and all steered requests on error
  - `notifyIdle()` wakes `send()` callers waiting for true session idleness
  - `dropRequest()` handles timeout cleanup for individual steered requests
  - Steered messages that miss the in-flight turn's boundaries are promoted to own the next turn

- **Content block extraction**: Moved `buildContentBlocks()` to a shared helper (used by both `send()` and `steer()`)

- **Agent integration**:
  - Added `steer` flag to `UserTurnRequest` to route mid-turn messages through `LiveSession.steer()` instead of the per-session queue
  - `drainPendingBatch()` now accepts a `steerable` flag; when true and a turn is in flight, messages bypass the queue and call `steer()`
  - Handles `STEER_MERGED` response by canceling the stream (the turn owner delivers the combined reply)
  - Without steering enabled, messages continue to queue normally (backward compatible)

- **Tests**: Comprehensive test suite in `tests/live-session.test.ts` covering:
  - Merging steered messages into the in-flight turn
  - Steered messages running as follow-up turns when they miss tool boundaries
  - `send()` waiting for promoted steered turns to finish
  - Stream failures rejecting all in-flight requests
  - Multiple steered messages merging and spilling independently
  - Integration tests in `tests/agent-integration.test.ts` validating end-to-end steering behavior

- **Config**: Added `steering: boolean` (default `false`) to enable the feature

## Implementation Details

- The mock SDK in tests eagerly pumps the input generator (like the real SDK), which is what enables mid-turn message injection — messages are consumed as soon as they're yielded, independent of turn state
- Steered message detection uses text matching: when a `user` event echoes back a pending steer's text mid-turn, it's marked as merged
- Timeout handling for steered requests is independent of the owner's timeout; each request has its own timer
- Session idleness tracking accounts for promoted steered turns that may run as follow-up turns after the current turn resolves

population.title: Unify global i18n provider and enable app-wide reactive translations
population.body:
### Motivation
- Dynamic, JS-generated UI (search results, news buttons/cards, studio window, album modal, etc.) was using hardcoded strings or local logic and therefore did not follow the same global translations as `data-i18n` markup. 
- The root cause was that dynamic surfaces did not read from a single, global language source and did not re-render when the language changed. 
- The goal is to centralize language access and make all user-facing text reactive to a single language selection without changing UI/UX or feature behavior.

### Description
- Added missing translation keys used by runtime-generated UI to `scripts/i18n.js` and made `window.AriyoI18n.t()` consistently resolve using the globally stored language, plus exposed `window.AriyoI18n.getLanguage()` for consumers. 
- Replaced hardcoded runtime strings with translation lookups for search UI in `scripts/main.js` (section headers, badges, empty state) and added a `ariyo:languageChanged` listener to re-render open search results. 
- Updated `scripts/news.js` and `scripts/studio-window.js` to use a small `i18nText` helper that calls the global `AriyoI18n.t()` so nav labels, aria labels, icon alt text, news tag/badges and studio window labels become translatable. 
- Added a `ariyo:languageChanged` listener in `scripts/ui.js` so open album modal content is repopulated when the language changes, and left static `data-i18n` markup untouched so existing layout and flow remain unchanged.

### Testing
- Syntax/parse checks were run with `node --check scripts/i18n.js scripts/main.js scripts/news.js scripts/studio-window.js scripts/ui.js` and returned no errors. 
- Automated script checks completed successfully and the updated i18n paths were exercised by the added `ariyo:languageChanged` listeners to ensure dynamic surfaces call the shared translation helper when re-rendering.

population.title: fix: restore active game lobby rejoin
population.body:
## Summary
- Replaces `get_my_current_table()` so active seated players keep a Lobby rejoin path for in-game tables, including Partners games between rounds.
- Adds Lobby recovery behavior for `already_seated_elsewhere` so failed join/create attempts refetch the current table and route players back when possible.
- Updates friendly error copy plus targeted rejoin/current-table checks.

## Risk level
High

## Risk areas touched
- Supabase RPCs
- Lobby/table lifecycle
- Partners mode rejoin behavior
- Private/public table seat conflict handling
- PostgREST schema cache reload

## Supabase migration notes
- Adds forward migration `20260613021808_fix_active_game_rejoin_path.sql`.
- Return contract for `get_my_current_table()` is unchanged: `table_id`, `table_name`, `game_mode`, `status`, `seat_number`, `joined_at`, `current_game_id`.
- The function remains `security definer`, uses `set search_path = public`, revokes public/anon execute, grants authenticated execute, and sends `NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema'`.
- Production project `ytizotohkxhsioxnmozd` was patched with this migration and schema cache reload so the live Player D rejoin path works before source alignment merges.
- Rollback consideration: reverting this migration would restore the dead-end for in-game seated players whose current game is active/round-finished. A rollback should replace `get_my_current_table()` with the prior definition and refresh PostgREST schema cache.

## Validation performed
- `npm run lint` passed.
- `npm run build` passed.
- `npm run test:run` passed: 63 files / 302 tests.
- `git diff --check` and `git diff --cached --check` passed.
- Production RPC verification: Player D `get_my_current_table()` now returns Partners Table 1 with seat 3 and game `411a5edc-b8d1-470c-9436-5ddc35301e5a`.
- Production browser smoke: `/lobby` shows the active-game banner and Rejoin Game routes to `/games/411a5edc-b8d1-470c-9436-5ddc35301e5a`.
- Production table smoke: private create/join works, invalid invite rejects, direct private `join_table` rejects, unauthorized private `get_table_room` rejects, private tables stay out of public lobby tables, public join/leave still works.

## Manual QA checklist
- [x] Player already seated in active Partners game sees Lobby current-table/rejoin banner.
- [x] Rejoin Game sends the player to the active game route.
- [x] Private table creation and invite joining work after the migration.
- [x] Public join/leave flow still works.
- [ ] After merge/deploy, verify the new Lobby fallback routes users after `already_seated_elsewhere` from Seat Me Now/create/private join.

## Follow-ups
- Keep an eye on production after merge for any stale browser bundle using the old error copy until Netlify finishes deploying main.

population.title: fix: restrict private table RPC grants
population.body:
## Summary

- Adds a forward Supabase migration that explicitly removes `anon` execute grants from restored private-table and table-room RPCs.
- Keeps authenticated execute grants for the app-facing RPCs the frontend uses.
- Removes direct authenticated exposure for private-table helper functions that should only run internally.
- Includes `NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema';` so PostgREST refreshes function permissions.

## Type of change

- Supabase migration / security hardening

## Risk level

High

## Risk areas touched

- Supabase RPC grants
- Private tables
- Table room access
- RLS helper function access
- PostgREST schema cache

## Production notes

Production had already been missing `20260613005450_restore_private_tables_current_rejoin.sql`; that migration was applied directly to project `ytizotohkxhsioxnmozd` and production history now includes it. During post-apply checks, Supabase security advisors and direct privilege checks showed explicit `anon` execute grants remained on restored functions, so this follow-up migration was applied to production as well and added here for GitHub source-of-truth alignment.

## Validation performed

- Confirmed production migration history includes:
  - `20260613005450_restore_private_tables_current_rejoin`
  - `20260613012000_revoke_anon_private_table_rpc_execute`
- Confirmed private-table schema objects and function definitions match the repository checklist.
- Confirmed `create_private_table(text)` and `join_private_table(text)` signatures match the frontend contract.
- Confirmed `anon` cannot execute private-table/table-room functions after this migration.
- Confirmed authenticated users can still create and join private tables.
- Confirmed unauthenticated private-table RPC calls fail with `42501 permission denied`.
- Confirmed production Lobby private-table create and join UI flows work without missing-RPC/PGRST errors.

## Commands run

- `npm run lint` — passed
- `npm run build` — passed
- `npm run test:run` — passed, 63 files / 301 tests
- `git diff --check` — passed

## Supabase migration / RPC / RLS notes

- This migration is non-destructive and changes only function grants.
- It preserves authenticated access to app-facing RPCs:
  - `can_view_game_table(uuid)`
  - `create_private_table(text)`
  - `join_private_table(text)`
  - `join_table(uuid)`
  - `sit_at_table(uuid, integer)`
  - `get_table_room(uuid)`
  - `get_my_current_table()`
- It removes `anon` execute access from the same surface.
- It removes direct authenticated execution for internal helpers:
  - `normalize_private_invite_code(text)`
  - `generate_private_invite_code()`

## Manual QA checklist

- Log in to production.
- Open `/lobby`.
- Create a private table from the Private Tables panel.
- Verify the private room loads and shows an invite code.
- Join the room from a second authenticated test account using the invite code.
- Verify direct `join_table(private_table_id)` rejects with `private_invite_required`.
- Verify unauthorized `get_table_room(private_table_id)` rejects with `private_invite_required`.
- Verify private tables do not appear in public lobby table results.

## Rollback notes

- This migration only tightens function grants. Rollback would require restoring `anon` execute grants, which is not recommended.
- If an authenticated flow unexpectedly fails, first check function privileges and PostgREST schema cache, then re-grant authenticated execute for the affected app-facing RPC.

## Follow-ups

- Existing Supabase advisor warnings remain for other SECURITY DEFINER functions and unrelated draft-table RLS policy gaps. Those should be handled in a separate security-hardening pass, not mixed into this private-table production fix.

population.title: docs: make impeccable playbook model-robust
population.body:
## What

Makes [`docs/plan-impeccable-page-improvements.md`](docs/plan-impeccable-page-improvements.md) produce a more consistent result regardless of which model runs it. Builds on #670 (playbook) and #672 (verify-plan patches).

## Why

The playbook's scaffolding (preflight, bucketing, watchlist greps, testing, ship) is deterministic — same on any model. But two steps are pure judgment: the `critique`/`audit` **scores** and the `fix`/`polish` **craft**. Because the gate is "no dimension below 3/4" and the model *assigns* that 3, a more lenient (smaller) model enforces a lower bar — **self-evaluation coupling**: the grader is the worker, so it can't hold itself above its own ceiling.

## Changes

1. **New "Model robustness" section** — pin `critique`/`audit` + the confirm re-score to **Opus/Fable** (`model: 'opus'`) even when a smaller model runs fixes. Decouples the *bar* (grader) from the *craft* (worker).
2. **Prefer measurable gates** over self-scored 0–4 where computable: contrast ratio (4.5:1), 44px touch targets, 1.25 type-scale ratio, literal watchlist greps. These are model-invariant.
3. **Score calibration anchors** in Definition of done — concrete 0/2/3/4 states (theming worked example) so "3/4" means the same thing on any model.

Docs-only.

population.title: fix(theme): clear stale theme-dark class so light-mode hover isn't near-black
population.body:
## The real root cause (PR #666 was a red herring)

Interactive elements (Get Directions, View on Google Maps, Publish/Download — any `hover:bg-accent` element) fill **near-black on hover in light mode when the OS is in dark mode**. PR #666 changed `color-scheme` and didn't fix it because **color-scheme was never the cause**.

`<html>` carries a **trio** of theme classes that must stay in sync:

| Class | Drives |
|---|---|
| `theme-light` / `theme-dark` | accent-color token blocks in `index.css` (`html[data-accent='clay'].theme-dark { --accent: #2a2520 }`) + scoring tokens |
| `dark` | Tailwind's `darkMode: 'class'` **and** the core surface tokens (`.dark { --background … }`) |

The accent blocks match on **both** `.dark` and `.theme-dark`. The core surface block matches **only** `.dark`.

`ThemeContext` (the provider actually mounted in `main.tsx`, driving the header sun/moon toggle) toggled **only `.dark`** and never touched `theme-dark`/`theme-light`.

### Reproduction trace (OS=dark, then toggle app to light via the header)
1. Boot OS=dark → `theme-init.js` sets `<html class="theme-dark dark" data-accent="clay">`.
2. Header toggle → `ThemeContext` removes **only** `.dark` → `<html class="theme-dark" data-accent="clay">`.
3. `--background` resolves **light** (`.dark` gone) but `html[data-accent='clay'].theme-dark` forces `--accent: #2a2520` (near-black). Every `hover:bg-accent` element fills near-black.

This is exactly why it only happens with **OS=dark + app=light**, and why VenueMap was a red herring — any `hover:bg-accent` element is affected.

## Fix

Route every applier through one shared `applyThemeClasses(root, isDark)` helper that always rewrites the full trio (`remove theme-light/theme-dark/dark` → add the correct pair). `ThemeContext` and `settingsStore` now both use it, so `theme-dark ⇔ dark` always holds. `theme-init.js` already did the right thing.

## Tests

`themeClasses.test.ts` — 5 tests pinning the invariant, including the regression case: **a stale `theme-dark` must not survive a switch to light**.

- `pnpm typecheck` ✅ 24/24
- `themeClasses.test.ts` ✅ 5/5
- settings/store suites ✅ 94/94
- eslint ✅ clean

## Verification note

Verified via the unit-test invariant (a pure class-state function). The Preview MCP is pinned to the main repo, not this worktree, so a browser screenshot here would not exercise the change; the bug is purely `<html>` class state + CSS cascade, fully covered by the regression test.

## Follow-up (out of scope)

There are still **four** theme systems (`ThemeContext`, `EnhancedThemeContext`, `theme-provider`, `settingsStore`) and two localStorage keys (`theme` vs `myK9Q_settings`). Only `ThemeContext` + `settingsStore` are live; the value-level disagreement between their two keys can still cause a boot flicker (separate, lower severity). Worth a consolidation pass per CLAUDE.md's "consolidate, don't duplicate."

population.title: Agent bridge: Proof-style live sessions via map serve
population.body:
## What this is

Mission 2, workstream 2 — the "bring your agent" flow rebuilt from research on Proof's actual code (`EveryInc/proof-sdk` clone study), agent-snippet ergonomics, and transport feasibility, then adversarially reviewed by three lenses (security / simplicity / agent-UX) before a line was written. RFC with candidates, decision, and full review dispositions: `outputs/audit/agent-bridge-rfc.md`.

**The flow:** DM opens a map → Agent panel shows a 12-line bootstrap snippet (no secrets in it) → agent starts `npm run map -- serve --map <file> --daemon`, which mints a 128-bit write token and prints it in the agent's own terminal → agent loops GET `/map` → edit → PUT `/map` per `docs/agent-bridge.md` → edits land in the DM's browser in ~2s, attributed (`ai:<name>`), schema-validated, revision-counted, re-scored. The map file on disk stays the source of truth.

**Key design calls** (all argued in the RFC): 3 routes, not 8; full-document PUTs, not JSON Patch; token minted by the bridge, never in the snippet/argv/clipboard; reads tokenless but Host+Origin-allowlisted; hard schema input bounds as a security boundary (a few-byte `width:100000` map used to hang scoring everywhere — now rejected in 7ms, with a regression test); editing locked in the workbench during live sessions; old file-watch flow (and its clobber bug + hardcoded `/Users/toby` prompt) deleted.

## Gate status

| Gate | Target | Result |
|---|---|---|
| E2E under Playwright (join → edit → live update → score recompute) | pass | **9/9 PASSED** (`outputs/audit/m2/bridge-e2e.ts`, evidence shot included) |
| Security checklist (RFC, incl. all adversarial-review additions) | all checked | **all checked** — input bounds, no-token-in-snippet, Host+Origin allowlists, actor grammar, write mutex + mtime guard, body cap, 127.0.0.1 bind, TTL, threat model stated |
| /agent page judged | ≥8 | **8.6** (fixes applied post-judge) |
| Docs + CLAUDE.md CLI contract | updated | `docs/agent-bridge.md` (new), `docs/agent.md`, `.well-known/agent.json`, CLAUDE.md |
| lint · test · build · export:smoke | green | green (17/17 tests — one new) |

## Deliberately not done (documented in the RFC)

- Hosted adapter (same 3 routes as Vercel functions + TTL'd KV) — designed, not built; no new paid services tonight.
- Browser→bridge write-back (DM edits flowing to the agent live) — V1.5; needs a paired-write design now that the browser holds no token.
- SSE — polling at 1.5s matches Proof's own public-SDK baseline; upgrade path documented.
- Safari from the hosted site — WebKit still blocks https→localhost; dev server works, stated honestly on /agent.

population.title: fix(issues): allow scoped recovery owner restore patch
population.body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip is the app Blockcast uses to coordinate AI agents, issue ownership, recovery actions, and board/operator interventions.
> - The affected subsystem is issue mutation authorization in `server/src/routes/issues.ts`.
> - Source-scoped recovery actions can assign a recovery owner to restore liveness on a specific source issue.
> - Before this PR, that recovery owner could be rejected by the generic issue boundary/assignee gate before the later recovery-action authority check ran.
> - The practical failure was a stale blocked source issue that the recovery owner could not clear, leaving QA retry work stranded.
> - This pull request adds a narrow pre-gate exception only for source-issue restoration patches owned by the active recovery action.
> - The benefit is live recovery without granting broad cross-agent mutation rights.

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

Paperclip refs: BLO-10219, BLO-10222.

## What happened?

A source-scoped recovery owner can be responsible for restoring a source issue but still receive `403 Issue is outside this actor's authorization boundary` or another cross-agent mutation denial before recovery-action authority is evaluated. This blocks recovery flows where the owner only needs to clear a stale `blocked` state with no blockers or return the issue to the original assignee for retry.

## Expected behavior

The active recovery owner can perform the minimal restoration on the scoped source issue, while normal content edits and unrelated mutations remain denied.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create or use a source issue assigned to one agent with an active source-scoped recovery action owned by a different agent.
2. As the recovery owner, attempt to patch the source issue only to clear stale `blocked` state with no blockers or return it to the expected owner.
3. Observe that the generic issue mutation gate rejects the request before recovery-action authority is applied.

## Paperclip version or commit

Reproduced against `master` before this PR; fixed in PR head `e207b687778e32c89e4b82bf705de3eb75643fd4`.

## Deployment mode

Self-hosted server / Paperclip production coordination instance.

## What Changed

- Added a scoped recovery-owner restore predicate for `PATCH /issues/:id`.
- Allowed the predicate to bypass the initial issue mutation gate only when the active recovery action owner is patching its exact source issue.
- Restricted the exception to restoration fields: `status: todo`, clearing `blockedByIssueIds`, returning assignee to the current/original return owner, and optional comment/follow-up flags.
- Reused the early recovery-action read for the later authority check to avoid inconsistent decisions.
- Added regression coverage for the allowed stale-block clear and a denied normal issue content edit.

## Verification

- `pnpm exec vitest run server/src/__tests__/issue-agent-mutation-ownership-routes.test.ts`

population.title: Add ESLint-based cyclomatic complexity fitness gate with ratcheted baseline
population.body:
This PR adds a new architectural fitness function to enforce cyclomatic complexity as a CI gate. It follows the existing `test/fitness` ratchet pattern so complexity can improve over time but cannot regress silently.

- **What was added**
  - New fitness test: `test/fitness/complexity.test.js`
  - Measures max cyclomatic complexity across `src/` using ESLint’s built-in `complexity` rule (`--format json`) and parses all reported complexity scores.
  - Logs measured value on every run for trend visibility.

- **Ratchet behavior**
  - Reads `test/fitness/baselines.json` and enforces `measured <= baselines.complexity.floor`.
  - Bootstraps `complexity` once when missing using:
    - `{ floor: measured, target: measured, measured }`
  - Does not rewrite the baseline on normal passing runs.
  - Fails fast on invalid/corrupt baseline (`non-numeric complexity.floor`).

- **Execution scope and safety**
  - Resolves scan root at runtime (`src/` if present, otherwise `.`).
  - Explicitly excludes `test/` and `node_modules/`.
  - Wraps ESLint invocation/parsing with descriptive failure errors to avoid silent passes on tool/config issues.

- **Baseline update**
  - Added `complexity` entry to `test/fitness/baselines.json` with the current measured floor.

population.title: Add knip-based dead-code fitness ratchet
population.body:
Closes #8

Adds a dead-code fitness gate using `knip` so unused files/exports in `src/` are measured automatically and cannot regress. The implementation follows the existing fitness-test ratchet pattern: bootstrap once, then enforce the stored floor on later runs.

- **Dependency + scope**
  - Adds exact `knip` devDependency and lockfile entries.
  - Configures `knip` in `package.json` to analyze `src/**/*.js` with `src/server.js` as the entrypoint.
  - Excludes `test/**`, `automation/**`, and `node_modules/**` so the metric reflects production code only.

- **Fitness function**
  - Adds `test/fitness/dead-code.test.js` with the `@fitness:dead-code` marker.
  - Runs `npx knip --reporter json`, parses JSON output even when `knip` exits non-zero, and counts unused `files` + `exports` under `src/`.
  - Keeps logging structured and count-only via `[fitness] dead-code measured: <n>`.

- **Ratchet baseline**
  - Extends `test/fitness/baselines.json` with a `dead-code` entry.
  - Bootstraps `floor`, `target`, and `measured` on first run.
  - Leaves `baselines.json` unchanged on later passing runs, so the floor only moves by intentional edit.

```js
if (!baselines['dead-code']) {
  baselines['dead-code'] = { floor: measured, target: measured, measured };
  fs.writeFileSync(BASELINES_PATH, `${JSON.stringify(baselines, null, 2)}\n`, 'utf-8');
  return;
}

expect(measured).to.be.at.most(
  floor,
  `Dead-code count ${measured} exceeds floor ${floor}. Remove unused exports in src/ — do not raise the floor in baselines.json.`
);
```

Bootstraps a Node.js/Express REST API from an empty repo, implementing secure CRUD for movies, actors, characters, and reviews. Upgrades Mongoose from `8.1.1` to `8.9.5` to patch a search injection vulnerability (affects `>= 8.0.0-rc0 < 8.9.5`).

## Core API
- Express 4.x with Helmet (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options DENY, nosniff), CORS allowlist, 100kb body limit, `x-powered-by` disabled
- Mongoose models: `Movie` (embedded cast), `Actor`, `Character` (referential integrity), `Review` (one-per-user-per-movie), `User` (bcrypt cost 12, `select: false` on sensitive fields)
- Routes: `/api/auth`, `/api/movies`, `/api/actors`, `/api/characters`, `/api/reviews`, nested `GET /api/movies/:movieId/reviews` with average rating aggregation

- **JWT RS256** — 15min access tokens + rotating refresh tokens with reuse detection; `alg:none` rejection via explicit `algorithms: ['RS256']`
- **RBAC** — deny-by-default `authorize(...roles)` middleware; viewer/user/admin enforced per route; IDOR prevention on review mutations (returns 404 to avoid existence confirmation)
- **Injection prevention** — `stripNoSqlOperators` removes `$`-prefixed keys from `req.body`/`req.query` globally; `stripHtml` in all model pre-save hooks
- **Rate limiting** — global 100 req/15min, auth endpoints 10 req/15min, write operations 30 req/15min
- **Audit logging** — Winston with PII masking (passwords, tokens, partial email `u***@domain.com`); structured security events (`AUTH_LOGIN_FAILURE`, `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, etc.)

- "mongoose": "8.1.1"
+ "mongoose": "8.9.5"

population.title: Consolidate cron scheduler setup into `BaseJob`
population.body:
Cron scheduling logic was duplicated across job implementations, which made scheduler behavior inconsistent and harder to evolve. This change centralizes the cron mechanism in `BaseJob` and has cron-enabled jobs declare only their schedule.

- **What changed**
  - Added `cronPattern?: string` to `BaseJob`.
  - Moved scheduler provisioning into `BaseJob.init()`:
    - If `cronPattern` is set, `init()` calls `queue.upsertJobScheduler(...)`.
    - Scheduler naming is standardized as ``${job.id}-repeat``.
    - Job payload remains normalized as `{ job: this.id }`.

- **Job-level refactor**
  - `AutoImportJob` now sets `cronPattern = env.autoImportCron` and no longer owns scheduler setup code.
  - `BudgetSumUpJob` now sets `cronPattern = env.budgetSumUpCron` and no longer owns scheduler setup code.

- **Behavioral impact**
  - Cron-enabled jobs keep their existing runtime logic; only scheduler registration moved to shared infrastructure.
  - Non-cron jobs are unaffected (`BaseJob.init()` is a no-op when `cronPattern` is undefined).

```ts
// BaseJob
readonly cronPattern?: string

async init(): Promise<void> {
  if (!this.cronPattern) return
  await queue.upsertJobScheduler(
    `${this.id}-repeat`,
    { pattern: this.cronPattern },
    { name: this.id, data: { job: this.id } },
  )
}

// Cron-enabled job
override readonly cronPattern = env.autoImportCron
```

population.title: Fix TypeError on corrupt Firebase data with dangling line references
population.body:
Application crashes when Firebase data contains line entries with `next` properties pointing to non-existent line IDs. Recursive traversal attempts to access properties on `undefined`.

## Changes

**Added null guards in recursive line traversal:**
- `render()` method's `next()` function now validates line existence before use
- `getSuggestion()` method's `iterate()` function now validates line existence before recursion
- Added console warnings to surface data inconsistencies for debugging

## Example

Before:
```javascript
if (line.next) next(this.state.script.lines[line.next], line.next);
```

After:
```javascript
if (line.next && this.state.script.lines[line.next]) next(this.state.script.lines[line.next], line.next);
```

Prevents crash when `this.state.script.lines[line.next]` is undefined.

population.title: Add migration dry-run tooling and edges polymorphic endpoints
population.body:
## Summary

This PR lands two interconnected deliverables from the WBS audit's open-leaves resolution:

1. **Migration dry-run tooling** (`scripts/migration-dry-run.sh`, GitHub workflow, Makefile target) — a parameterized drill that applies pending migrations against an isolated Postgres instance seeded with production-sized data, timing the candidate apply and validating data integrity.

2. **Edges table polymorphic endpoints migration** (`0017_edges_polymorphic_endpoints.sql`) — widens the `edges` table to support annotation endpoints alongside node endpoints, with per-endpoint XOR CHECK constraints and NULLS NOT DISTINCT uniqueness semantics.

## Key Changes

### Migration Dry-Run Tooling
- **`scripts/migration-dry-run.sh`**: A 179-line bash script that:
  - Boots an isolated Postgres in its own compose project (alternate host port, separate volume)
  - Extracts and applies baseline migrations from `BASE_REF` (default `origin/main`) via the real `node-pg-migrate` runner
  - Seeds production-sized data (configurable: ~1k users, ~50k nodes, ~50 sessions, ~200k events) using `generate_series`
  - Applies candidate migrations from the working tree, timed against a configurable budget (default 120s)
  - Validates that seeded data survived and the `pgmigrations` ledger matches the on-disk file count
  - Cleans up (down -v) on success and failure alike

- **`.github/workflows/migration-dry-run.yml`**: On-demand workflow dispatch (manual trigger + temporary branch push for this task's execution) that runs the dry-run on a GitHub runner with full Docker support.

- **`Makefile` target**: `make migration-dry-run` with help text; env knobs documented in the script header.

- **`docs/runbooks/release.md`**: Updated migration checklist to reference the concrete command for pre-release drills.

### Edges Polymorphic Endpoints Migration
- **`apps/server/migrations/0017_edges_polymorphic_endpoints.sql`**: 77-line forward-only migration that:
  - Makes `source_node_id` and `target_node_id` nullable (endpoints become polymorphic)
  - Adds `source_annotation_id` and `target_annotation_id` as nullable FKs to `annotations` with ON DELETE RESTRICT
  - Adds two named XOR CHECK constraints (`edges_source_endpoint_xor`, `edges_target_endpoint_xor`) to enforce exactly-one endpoint per side
  - Replaces the three-column inline UNIQUE constraint with a five-column NULLS NOT DISTINCT unique index over the full endpoint tuple
  - Adds partial lookup indexes on the annotation-endpoint columns (NULL on every node–node edge, so partial avoids bloat)

- **Behavior test coverage**: 6 new scenarios in `tests/behavior/migrations/edges.feature` + matching step definitions in `tests/behavior/steps/edges.steps.ts`:
  - Node-to-annotation and annotation-to-node edge inserts succeed
  - Both-set and neither-set endpoint shapes are rejected by XOR CHECKs
  - Duplicate annotation-endpoint edges are rejected (NULLS NOT DISTINCT pin)
  - Foreign-key violation on non-existent annotation reference

- **Test helpers**: Added `annB` UUID to `TEST_UUIDS` for FK violation scenarios.

## Implementation Details

- **Readiness gate**: `/readyz` reads pre-recorded migration gate state (set at boot in `index.ts`) rather than re-deriving it per probe, ensuring fast responses
- **Metrics**: Low-cadence (60s) interval emission as structured log lines so they appear in Railway's log search without a separate metrics pipeline
- **Sentry**: Structurally no-ops when `SENTRY_DSN` is absent/empty — dev/CI/compose stacks never arm it; operator arms production via Railway Variable
- **Migration linter**: Regex-based (not SQL parser) with per-rule allow-markers requiring non-empty justifications; enforces two-tag dance for destructive changes
- **Load test**: Three phases — ingest throughput (concurrent synthetic sessions), concurrent audience (WS subscribers + catch-up latency), live fan-out ceiling (sequence-gated proposes)
- **Rollback**: Image rollback only (no migration reversal); prior image must tolerate newer schema — the invariant the linter enforces

All work is gated by ADR 0033 (observability), ADR 0034 (releases), ADR 0020 (migrations), and ADR 0041 (synthetic sessions).

## What changed
This PR adds a repo-owned `npm run db:lint` wrapper for `supabase db lint` and documents the supported verification paths for Codex and local development.

It also updates the tool-check output and verification docs so issue `#10` no longer relies on an implicit assumption that `supabase db lint --local` is always reachable from the Codex sandbox.

The current Codex environment does not guarantee a working local Supabase stack:
- Docker is unavailable here.
- Localhost access to the expected Supabase Postgres port may be sandbox-blocked.
- In some worktrees, the repo-local Supabase CLI may not yet be installed.

Without an explicit wrapper and docs, `supabase db lint` fails opaquely and leaves issue `#10` blocked on environment details instead of a clear verification contract.

## Impact
- Contributors can run `SUPABASE_DB_URL=postgresql://... npm run db:lint` against a disposable or dev-only database.
- When a local Supabase stack is reachable, the wrapper still supports `supabase db lint --local`.
- Codex and orchestration work now have a documented, defensible fallback verification path.

- `npm run test`
  - Passed.
- `npm run verify`
  - Passed.

## Root cause
The blocker is environmental rather than application logic: `supabase db lint --local` depends on external local database availability that this sandbox does not guarantee.

population.title: Add owner-scoped SELECT RLS policy for `artifact_ledger` (defense-in-depth)
population.body:
This PR adds the missing RLS owner-read policy on `public.artifact_ledger` as a minimal forward-only hardening step before durable artifact persistence (FASE 2). It preserves current backend behavior (`service_role` with `BYPASSRLS`) and does not change runtime flows.

- **RLS migration (minimal, idempotent)**
  - Added `supabase/migrations/20260612_add_artifact_ledger_select_owner_policy.sql`.
  - Defines only one policy: `artifact_ledger_select_owner`.
  - Scope is explicit and narrow: `FOR SELECT` + `TO authenticated`.
  - Uses safe TEXT-compatible comparison: `user_id = (auth.uid())::text`.
  - Includes rollback comment with `DROP POLICY IF EXISTS ...`.

- **Security behavior preserved**
  - No `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE` policies were added.
  - No table/column/type changes (`user_id` remains `TEXT`).
  - `user_id IS NULL` rows remain non-visible to `authenticated` (fail-closed).
  - No changes to `api/`, frontend, providers, Serginho, or execution/runtime toggles.

- **Governance/docs updates**
  - Added dated top entry in `CHECKLIST.md` with scope, invariants, and rollback SQL.
  - Added concise `CHANGELOG.md` security note under Unreleased.

```sql
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS artifact_ledger_select_owner ON public.artifact_ledger;

CREATE POLICY artifact_ledger_select_owner
  ON public.artifact_ledger
  FOR SELECT
  TO authenticated
  USING (user_id = (auth.uid())::text);
```

population.title: feat(catalog): replace 動手做 with 精選 30k+ catalog walk
population.body:
## Summary

Replaces the LLM-invented 「動手做」 (ideation) tab with a new 「精選」 (catalog) section: a daily walk of the catalog of 30k+ star AI projects, deduplicated across days so each day surfaces ≤10 repos the reader hasn't seen yet (AI-first, with standout general dev tools). Once the catalog is walked it trickles to newcomers crossing the bar.

**Why:** ideation was synthesizer-invented and low-signal; the catalog walk surfaces genuinely-proven projects an AI builder may have missed.

## How it works

- **Fetcher** (`github-catalog`): queries `stars:>=30000` across core AI topics + a general bucket, excludes already-shown repos via `loadSeenSet()`, emits a stars-ranked candidate pool → `data/staging/feeds-catalog.json`. Honest `ok` degradation when GitHub search errors.
- **Dedup ledger** (`data/seen-repos.json`, committed to the `data` branch): read at Stage 1 (local → `git show origin/data` → `[]`); only the ≤10 **shown** picks are appended at Stage 4 (idempotent, error-isolated), so fetched-but-unshown repos stay eligible. Mechanical dedup state — distinct from the retired `data/memory.json`.
- **Curator** (`curate.catalog`): a 5th Haiku curated section wired as a **non-critical optional** DAG stage — shares only the `collect` dep, only `merge` orders after it, so a catalog failure degrades and never blocks the pipeline.
- **Render**: the `精選` tab takes 動手做's slot (2nd); category-filtered (AI 相關 / 通用精選) with chips shown only when non-empty.
- **Ideation removed end-to-end**: editorial/report schemas, `IdeaItem`, merge, repair-editorial, faithfulness guard, `synthesizer.md` + `quality.md`, the **runtime** synth-prompt contract (`build-synthesizer-prompt.mjs`), templates, and all affected tests.

Star threshold (30000), pool sizes, and topics are config (`themes/<theme>/sources.yaml` + `interests.yaml`). Spec/plan: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-08-catalog-walk-design.md` + `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-08-catalog-walk.md` (gitignored).

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` — 393 pass (new: seen-repos ledger, github-catalog pool shaping, catalog schema, merge composition, DAG non-blocking, runtime-prompt ideation guard)

population.body:
## What

The 技術 (tech) tab's benchmark items linked to fabricated leaderboard URLs. The OCRBench item linked to `github.com/Yuliang-Liu/Multimodal-OCR` → **404** (the real repo is `.../MultimodalOCR`, no hyphen).

## Root cause

Leaderboard staging items carry only rankings (`bench` / `top_5_today` / diffs) — **no url**. The tech curator was nonetheless asked to supply a "link to leaderboard" with no source, so it **hallucinated a different url every day**:

| date | fabricated OCRBench url |
|---|---|
| 06-01 | huggingface.co/spaces/allenai/OCRBench |
| 06-02 | huggingface.co/spaces/Xorbix/OCR-Benchmark |
| 06-04 | huggingface.co/spaces/harmful/ocrbench |
| 06-05 | github.com/royalknight56/OCRBench |
| 06-06 | huggingface.co/spaces/ocr-research/ocrbench |
| 06-08 | github.com/Yuliang-Liu/Multimodal-OCR (404) |

All three benchmarks were affected (BFCL invented `huggingface.co/spaces/anybodys/BFCL`). A stale prompt also listed MTEB/PinchBench as active, so the curator sometimes invented whole **ghost benchmark items** (a fabricated "MTEB Leaderboard: Claude dominates embeddings" with no backing data).

## Fix

- `src/lib/leaderboard-urls.js` — single source of truth: each bench → its hand-verified leaderboard page (all 200-verified) + `benchOf()` to identify an item by `bench` field or title token.
- `leaderboard-html.js` — stamps the canonical url onto each staging item.
- `merge.js` — deterministic cure of `tech.benchmarks`: canonical url for a known bench, url **stripped** for an unknown/ghost bench, so a fabricated link can never reach the page (same cure-don't-abort philosophy as the existing `source_link` cure).
- tech curator prompt — corrected active-benchmark list (BFCL / SWE-bench Verified / OCRBench only) and forbids inventing benchmarks or URLs.

`benchOf` unit tests + `composeReport` cure tests (canonical override, ghost-url strip, no input mutation).

population.title: fix(sources): repair hf-daily-papers, arxiv-cs-ai, mops degradations
population.body:
## What

Repairs the three collect-source degradations from the 2026-06-07 production
run, each fixed at its root cause.

| Source | Nature | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `hf-daily-papers` | Data-format / validation — RSSHub fetched 30 items, all rejected | Add `normalizeArxivPaper` in `rsshub.js`, routed by `ctx.itemType`; parse paper_id from the HF url → `arxiv.org/abs` |
| `arxiv-cs-ai` | Transient arXiv 429 + a tier-1 fallback that never produced items | Exponential-backoff retry on 429/503 in the arxiv-rss provider (primary cause); teach `extractArxivPaper` the arxiv-listing markdown format (tier-1) |
| `mops-disclosure` | Low-frequency source; weekend/holiday empty mis-flagged degraded | `threshold: 0` so a successful empty fetch stays healthy; a real provider error still fails |

## Why

- **hf-daily-papers**: the generic rsshub normalizer emits a shape (`description` / singular `author` / `category`) that can never satisfy the `arxiv-paper` item schema, so the validating wrapper dropped all 30 items even though the fetch succeeded.
- **arxiv-cs-ai**: tier-0 (export.arxiv.org API) intermittently 429s; on those days the whole source was lost because tier-1 (jina on arxiv.org/list) only recognised the HuggingFace markdown format.
- **mops-disclosure**: `threshold` defaulting to 1 conflated "zero matching disclosures" (normal on weekends) with "fetch failed", polluting `metadata.degraded`.

## Tests

`tests/source-fixes.test.js` exercises each fix against real production code: rsshub normalization through the validating wrapper, the dual-format extractor, 429 retry / give-up / no-retry behaviour, the registry threshold, and runChain's threshold-0 semantics.

population.title: feat(ops): production-run --recover-from <stage>
population.body:
## Why

Recovering today's failed run (#99's Stage 4 merge abort) exposed an ergonomic gap in the production runner. The only command that runs the **full publish tail** (validate → verify remote → dispatch Pages → write `latest.json` so the monitor clears) is `production-run.js run`, and it hard-coded `run.sh --full`.

`--full` re-runs **Stage 1 collect**, which rewrites `data/staging/metadata.json` — the freshness anchor `satisfied()` compares downstream outputs against (`src/pipeline/satisfied.js`). So re-collect invalidates *every* downstream stage as `stale`, forcing a complete re-run. That is the correct guard when source data is refetched (you must not staple old curated/editorial onto a fresh fetch), but it meant recovering from a **deterministic** stage failure (merge is pure Node) re-spent ~$2.4 of LLM work that had already succeeded.

The cheap path — `run.sh --recover-from <stage>` — already reuses upstream work (it never touches collect), but it stops at commit: no dispatch, no `latest.json` update. So the two capabilities were split across two tools.

## What

`production-run.js run --recover-from STAGE` joins them:

- Drives `run.sh --recover-from STAGE` instead of `--full` → the sequencer resumes from `STAGE`, reusing already-finished upstream stages (no re-collect, no re-spent LLM).
- Keeps the **same publish tail** (validate → verify remote → dispatch Pages → write state), so the monitor flips to `succeeded`.
- Rejects an unknown stage up front (exit 2, lists valid stages) instead of letting an operator typo surface as a buried failed run + monitor alert.

So the recovery that today cost a full re-run becomes:

```
node src/ops/production-run.js run --state-dir D --recover-from merge
```

## Implementation / tests

- `run.sh` argv+env construction extracted into a pure, exported `buildRunArgs()` — unit-tested across full / skip-push / recover-from without spawning. Note: recover-from passes `SKIP_PUSH` via **env** (run.sh's `publish_unless_skip` reads it from the environment, not a positional flag).
- `parseArgs` exported + parses `--recover-from`; tests cover the new parse + the buildRunArgs matrix.
- `npm run lint` ✓ · `npm test` ✓ (362 passed) · CLI smoke: bad stage → exit 2 with the valid-stage list.
- Docs: CLAUDE.md "How to Run" row + the file header usage updated.

> Independent of #99 (the schema-drift fix). This is the operability follow-up that makes future deterministic-stage recoveries cheap.

population.title: fix: move feeds_sections out of source_health
population.body:
## Problem

Today's Hermes production run (2026-06-06) **failed at Stage 4 (merge)**:

```
[merge-report] schema validation failed:
  - meta.source_health.feeds_sections.ok: Invalid input: expected boolean, received undefined
  - meta.source_health.feeds_sections.count: Invalid input: expected number, received undefined
```

All upstream stages (collect → curate ×4 → context → synthesize) succeeded; only the pure-Node merge aborted.

## Root cause — schema drift from the condense cutover (#90–#95)

- `feeds_sections` (a per-section item-count breakdown, e.g. `{pulse:245, market:193, tech:54, shipped:53}`) was added **inside `metadata.sources`** (`src/collect.js`), and the **staging** schema was updated to accept it there — so Stage 1 validated fine.
- Stage 4 `report-meta.js` copies `metadata.sources` **verbatim** into `meta.source_health`.
- The **report** schema types `source_health` as a uniform `record(string, {ok, count})`. `feeds_sections` has neither field → validation fails.

The two contracts drifted: the staging side gained `feeds_sections`, but the report side / the wholesale copy never did. It only detonated on the **first production run after the cutover** (#94 made section slices the sole feed staging; #91 introduced `feeds_sections`). Tests missed it because none routed a `sources` object containing `feeds_sections` through `aggregateMeta` and validated the result against the report meta schema.

## Fix

- **`feeds_sections` is a sibling of `sources`, not a member** — moved to a top-level staging field (`src/collect.js`, `src/schemas/staging.js`) and surfaced as a dedicated `meta.feeds_sections` in the report (`src/lib/report-meta.js`, `src/schemas/report.js`). `source_health` is once again a uniform `{ok,count}` map.
- **Hardened `staging.sources` with `.strict()`** — any future non-`{ok,count}` field now aborts at **Stage 1** (cheapest layer) instead of after ~20 min of LLM work at Stage 4.
- **Added the missing integration test**: `aggregateMeta → ReportMetaSchema` (the gate that actually failed), plus a strict-rejection test.

## Verification

- `npm run lint` ✓ · `npm test` ✓ (358 passed)
- Re-ran Stage 4 against the failed run's staging → `data/reports/2026-06-06.json` composes and **passes `npm run validate:report`**; `source_health` clean, `feeds_sections` surfaced separately.

> ⚠️ Production runs from `main`, so this needs to merge **before tomorrow's 07:00 run** or it fails identically. Today's report is recovered separately (republished from the already-built staging).

population.title: fix: tracked-directory handling (apply/restore/verify) + bare-init .gitignore
population.body:
## Summary
Bugs found by **live sandbox testing** — building the CLI and running real `tuck` commands against throwaway fake homes (`HOME=$(mktemp -d)`), which the 1200+ mocked unit tests missed because they only ever used **single files**. Each fix is verified by a real end-to-end run **and** a regression test that now exercises directory entries.

### Tracked directories crashed with EISDIR (`~/.config/*`, `~/.ssh` are common)
- **`apply`**: both materialization loops read `repoPath` as text (secret-resolution / smart-merge) → `EISDIR` on a directory, leaving a **partial apply** (the file applied, the directory didn't, then it errored). New `applyDirectoryEntry()` copies the tree + applies recorded perms.
- **`restore`**: `restoreFiles`/`restoreFilesWithResolver` (placeholder restoration) `readFile`'d every restored path; now skip directory paths.
- **`verify --apply`**: the dry-apply read `repoPath` as a file; now copies dir trees and diffs by directory checksum.

### `verify --apply --root <dir>` ignored the user's `--root`
`--root` is a **global** option (resolved into the WriteContext by the preAction hook), so the verify subcommand's `options.root` is empty on a real CLI run — `--apply` was silently writing into a throwaway temp dir. Now it honors the global sandbox root for inspection.

### `init --bare` shipped no security `.gitignore`
The `.gitignore` (excludes `secrets.local.json` / keystore / backups) was only written by `createDefaultFiles`, which `--bare` skips — so secrets could be committed/pushed. Now always written via `ensureRuntimeArtifactsGitignored` (doctor `security.runtime-gitignore`: **fail → pass**, `18/1/1 → 20/0/0`).

## Verification
Live sandbox runs (init/add/status/list/verify/sync/restore/apply/secrets/doctor + cross-machine `file://` apply + `verify --apply --root`), real `~` never touched. `pnpm typecheck` clean · `pnpm lint` clean · `pnpm test` **1205 passing**.

population.body:
## Summary
Final wave — an efficiency win + the highest-risk coverage gaps. TDD throughout; memfs / sandboxed temp dirs only (never the real home).

### Performance — conservative file-hash short-circuit (single files only)
Avoid re-hashing **unchanged** single files on every `status`/`sync`/`verify` (a git/make-style mtime+size cache):
- `trackedFile` gains **optional** `sourceMtimeMs`/`sourceSize` — legacy entries parse byte-identical and fall back to full hashing.
- `fileTracking` records them for regular files (never directories).
- `stateModel.computeFileState` stats the live source first and reuses the recorded checksum **only** when `st.isFile() && size && mtimeMs` all match — otherwise hashes exactly as before.
- **Directories are never short-circuited** (a dir's own mtime doesn't change on a nested-file edit). The one accepted blind spot — a content change preserving *both* mtime and byte size — is the standard build-tool tradeoff, documented in the code.

### Test coverage (no src changes)
- **Keystore round-trip** (`tests/lib/keystore-roundtrip.test.ts`): real `FallbackKeystore` store→retrieve→delete with whitespace preserved byte-for-byte (no trim), Unicode/emoji, overwrite, missing→null, delete→null, cross-instance durability.
- **Non-GitHub e2e** (`tests/integration/provider-e2e.test.ts`): real git + temp dirs, **no GitHub/network** — (a) a non-GitHub repo applied end-to-end via the custom `file://` provider clone + the real `loadManifestFile` validator; (b) local-mode commits and **refuses** a push via `assertRemoteAvailable` (`LocalModeError`).

population.title: perf+fix: wave-4 — scan/sync perf, cache invalidation, template engine, files.ts
population.body:
## Summary
Wave 4 — efficiency + correctness. All perf changes are **behavior-preserving** (regression tests assert identical results); TDD throughout; memfs/temp only.

### Performance
- **scan/sync new-file detection** was O(detected × tracked) (a `getTrackedFileBySource` scan per detected file). New `manifest.buildSourceIndex()` builds a `source→{id,file}` Map once → O(1) lookups.
- **detect.ts** collapsed 3 serial syscalls/pattern (×~150 patterns) to one `stat` per path, probes run concurrently (`Promise.all`), order + symlink-follow preserved.
- **`loadTuckignore`** was re-read per detected file (~150×) → hoisted above the loop via `isIgnoredInSet(preloadedSet, path)` (`isIgnored` now delegates to it).
- **sync change-application** carries the manifest id on each change + indexes tracked files once → removes per-change reload and linear `.find()` (O(changes × tracked)).
- **files.ts** `copyFileOrDir` directory branch walked the tree **3×** → one shared single-pass walker (`getDirectoryTreeStats`, size opt-in).

### Correctness
- **Cache invalidation:** `clearManifestCache()` after a clone in `init --from` and `apply`, `clearConfigCache()` after config writes — no run operates on a stale in-memory manifest/config.
- **Template engine:** a nested `{{tuck:else}}` under a **false** parent no longer leaks its body; inline nested `{{#if}}` uses a depth-balanced parser instead of greedy-matching the first `{{/if}}`.
- **files.ts** no-overwrite directory copy no longer silently **merges** into an existing target (throws `DESTINATION_EXISTS`) and preserves real error codes (`ENOSPC`/`ENOENT`) instead of masking them as permission errors.

**Deferred (noted):** file-hash mtime/size short-circuit (cross-cutting — its own focused PR) and lazy command imports (Commander-registration risk).

## Verification
`pnpm typecheck` clean · `pnpm lint` clean · `pnpm test` **1182 passing** (+33).

population.title: feat(provider): wave-3 — provider-neutral lifecycle (less GitHub coupling)
population.body:
## Summary
Wave 3 — reduce GitHub coupling so **GitLab / custom / local are first-class**. TDD throughout; all tests mock git/providers/network and use memfs (no real remote or home touched).

- **Clone safety:** `git.ts cloneRepo` now bounds clones with `timeout` (`GIT_OPERATION_TIMEOUTS.CLONE`) + `maxBuffer` — init/apply can't hang on a huge/wedged remote.
- **Local-mode push gating:** `push` **and** `sync` now call `assertRemoteAvailable(config.remote, 'push')` before every push, so a local-only repo refuses to push even when a stray git `origin` exists (was: pushed whenever an origin existed).
- **`setupRemoteForProvider`** (new `src/lib/remoteSetup.ts`): one provider-agnostic remote-setup flow used by **both** `init` and `config remote`. The init wizard's GitLab/custom branch no longer funnels through GitHub-only setup / `validateGitHubUrl` / hard-coded `github.com` — it uses the chosen provider's `validateUrl`/`buildRepoUrl`. GitHub init's auto-create path is preserved.
- **Provider-neutral `apply <source>`:** routes `custom:` / `file://` / full git URLs through the custom provider's bounded clone, and resolves a bare `owner/repo` via the **configured** provider's `buildRepoUrl` (then detected providers) instead of an unconditional `https://github.com/...` literal.
- **Cloned-manifest validation (security):** new `loadManifestFile()` runs `tuckManifestSchema.parse` on untrusted cloned/remote manifests in both `apply` and `init`, rejecting hostile shapes before use.

**Deferred (noted):** full `lib/github.ts` ↔ `providers/github.ts` dedup and the `runInteractiveInit` state-machine decomposition — both large, low user-value, higher risk.

## Verification
`pnpm typecheck` clean · `pnpm lint` clean · `pnpm test` **1141 passing** (+22).

population.body:
## Summary
Wave 2 of audit remediation — agent-surface completeness, the sandbox preview story, and platform/keystore hardening. TDD throughout; all tests run against memfs / sandboxed temp roots, **never the real home**.

### Agent-JSON completeness (P1)
- `secrets list/set/unset/path` gain `--json` (+ `--yes` on set). Each emits exactly one `{ok,command}` envelope; secret **values are never echoed** (`set` reads from `TUCK_SECRET_VALUE` to keep secrets out of argv/history).
- `restore` skipped-file warnings now route through `addJsonWarning` → surface in `envelope.warnings`.
- `add --plan/--dry-run` now runs the **full** `preparePathsForTracking` pipeline (category/secret/validation) so the plan matches a real run.

### Sandbox preview (P1/P2) — completes Layer 4 of the sandboxing design
- `verify --root <dir>`: confine write/preview targets under a dry-home sandbox (reads still use real home).
- `verify --apply`: **dry-apply diff** — runs the apply prepare pipeline into the sandbox (auto temp dir, always cleaned up), classifies each file `created|modified|unchanged`, surfaces `smartMerge` **conflicts** that plain apply silently discards, and reports any entry that **would escape the root** in `wouldEscapeRoot` (writing nothing). Emits `{root,changes,conflicts,wouldEscapeRoot}`.
- `doctor`: new **sandboxing** category with copy-pasteable OS-wrapper recipes (`sandbox-exec`/`bwrap`/landlock/container) + `--root` status.

### Keystore / platform (P2)
- Windows editor default → `notepad` (was `vim`/`vi` → ENOENT).
- Fallback keystore KDF mixes in a **per-install random 32-byte secret** (`~/.tuck/keystore.key`, 0600) so the file isn't derivable from machine info alone — **with a legacy-key fallback** so existing keystores stay decryptable across upgrade and migrate transparently on next write (**no data loss**; regression test included).
- Linux `isAvailable()` now requires a real session bus + bounded probe (headless/WSL → encrypted file keystore); Windows `isAvailable()` returns false by design (cmdkey can't retrieve) → clean fallback.

## Verification
`pnpm typecheck` clean · `pnpm lint` clean · `pnpm test` **1117 passing** (+30 new tests).

> Reviewer note: the per-install-secret KDF change is data-loss-sensitive on upgrade; the legacy-key fallback + migration test (`keystoreFallback.test.ts`) specifically guards existing users' stored secrets.

population.title: fix: honor explicit custom pricing for BYOK deployments (#30081)
population.body:
## Title
fix: honor explicit custom pricing for BYOK deployments (#30081)

## Relevant issues
Closes #30081

## What this fixes
Custom per-token pricing configured on a deployment (e.g. a BYOK `anthropic/*` wildcard route with `input_cost_per_token: 0`) was silently dropped in two situations:

1. **Cost-map reload wipes deployment pricing.** Deployment pricing is registered under the router model id in the process-global `litellm.model_cost`. When the model-cost map is reloaded (replaced wholesale), that entry disappears and cost calculation falls back to the *public* price of the canonical model — so a BYOK route priced at `0` is billed at full public rates.
2. **Per-request pricing poisons the shared entry.** Per-request custom pricing was registered against the shared canonical `litellm.model_cost` key, re-pricing the canonical model for the whole process and silently mis-billing all subsequent traffic.

## The fix
- **Thread explicit rates through the cost calculator.** Extracts the deployment's explicit `input_cost_per_token` / `output_cost_per_token` from `litellm_params` and passes them as `custom_cost_per_token`. `0` is treated as a valid rate.
- **Stop poisoning the canonical entry.** Skip overwriting `litellm.model_cost` for models that already resolve to known pricing; per-request rates are applied via the threaded `custom_cost_per_token` instead.

## Tests
`tests/test_litellm/test_custom_pricing_robustness.py` (20 tests)

---
